# MCP server

<!-- Generated by wabcut_command_docgen (src/command/mcp/src/McpDocs.cpp); do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: build\win-msvc\bin\wabcut_command_docgen.exe docs/commands.md docs/mcp.md -->

`wabcut-cli mcp` serves one project to external AI agents (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others) over the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). The tools are the typed edit commands of [docs/commands.md](commands.md): every edit is validated, previewable with `dryRun`, and one undo step. The server is local only: stdio, no network, no files besides the project.

## Protocol

* **Implemented revision: MCP 2026-07-28** (stateless: every request carries `_meta` `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `clientCapabilities`; `server/discover`; results carry `resultType`). Checked against <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28> on 2026-10-11.
* Clients that open with `initialize` get the handshake-based revisions **2025-11-25** and **2025-06-18** (the spec's dual-era server, "Versioning: Backward Compatibility"). The server answers with the requested revision when it serves it, otherwise with the newest one it serves; the client then decides whether to continue.
* Transport: stdio, one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per line, UTF-8. stdout carries only protocol messages; diagnostics go to stderr. JSON-RPC batches are not supported (removed from MCP in 2025-06-18).

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `server/discover` | Supported versions, capabilities (`tools`, `resources`), server info, instructions. |
| `initialize`, `notifications/initialized` | Legacy handshake (see above). |
| `ping` | Always answered. |
| `tools/list`, `tools/call` | The tools below; results carry `structuredContent` (matching each tool's `outputSchema`) and the same JSON as text. |
| `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read` | `wabcut://project/summary` and `wabcut://sequence/{id}`. |
| `notifications/cancelled` | Stops the running call at its next checkpoint (nothing is committed) or skips a queued request; no response is sent for it. |
| `notifications/progress` | Sent for calls with `_meta.progressToken`: once per batch step, per range of `timeline_removeSilences` and before a commit. `progress` counts up; there is no `total`. |

**Errors.** Protocol problems are JSON-RPC errors:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| -32700 | The line is not JSON. |
| -32600 | Not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request (bad `jsonrpc`, `id` or `method`), a batch array, a message over 4 MiB or nested deeper than 64. |
| -32601 | Unknown method. |
| -32602 | Bad params: missing `_meta` fields (2026-07-28) without a prior `initialize`, unknown tool, arguments not an object, unknown resource. |
| -32022 | `_meta` names a protocol version the server does not serve; `data.supported` lists the one it does. |
| -32603 | Internal error. |

Problems with a tool call itself (bad parameters, a stale revision, an edit the model refuses, a read-only server) come back as a normal result with `isError: true`. The text explains the problem, and `structuredContent.error` has `code`, `message` and `details`, so the model can correct itself.

## Setup

Run the server with `wabcut-cli mcp --project <file.wabcut>`:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--project <file>` | The project to serve (required). |
| `--allow-edit` | Enables the edit tools (`EditSequence`, `EditProject`), undo/redo and `project_save`. Without it the server is read-only. |
| `--allow-analysis` | Also serves the analysis commands (`MediaAnalysis`: `transcript.transcribe` with local transcription and the analysis cache, `audio.loudness`). They decode media and can run long: raise `--timeout-ms`. Network commands are never served. |
| `--allow-files` | Also serves the commands that read or write files (review packages, CDL and LUT files, `project.merge`, `lottie.import`, ...), confined to the project's folder: every path they are given must lie inside it once symlinks and junctions are resolved. Without it they are not listed and refused by name. `plugins.scan` (native code) is never served. |
| `--files-folder <dir>` | One more folder those commands may use (repeatable; implies `--allow-files`). |
| `--save-on-exit` | Saves the project when the client disconnects, if anything changed (needs `--allow-edit`). |
| `--autosave` | Saves after every change (needs `--allow-edit`). |
| `--timeout-ms <n>` | Longest a tool call may run (default 30000). |

Without a save flag, changes stay in memory until the agent calls `project_save`. Every save is atomic and keeps rotated `.bak` copies.

### Claude Desktop

Add to `claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\`, macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`), then restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wabcut": {
      "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Wabcut\\wabcut-cli.exe",
      "args": ["mcp", "--project", "C:\\Users\\me\\Videos\\Rough cut.wabcut", "--allow-edit", "--save-on-exit"]
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `--allow-edit` (and the save flag) for a read-only connection.

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add wabcut -- wabcut-cli mcp --project ./rough-cut.wabcut --allow-edit
```

or check a project-scoped `.mcp.json` into the repository:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wabcut": {
      "command": "wabcut-cli",
      "args": ["mcp", "--project", "rough-cut.wabcut", "--allow-edit"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

```
codex mcp add wabcut -- wabcut-cli mcp --project /home/me/rough-cut.wabcut --allow-edit
```

or in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.wabcut]
command = "wabcut-cli"
args = ["mcp", "--project", "/home/me/rough-cut.wabcut", "--allow-edit"]
```

Cursor and other clients use the same `mcpServers` JSON as Claude Desktop.

## Safety model

* **Read-only by default.** The client gets the `Read` capability. `--allow-edit` adds `EditSequence` and `EditProject`, `--allow-analysis` adds `MediaAnalysis`; `Network` commands are never served. Edit tools are not even listed on a read-only server; calling one anyway returns an `isError` result (`PermissionDenied`) that tells the user to restart with `--allow-edit`.
* **AI models.** Read tools that run a local model (`search.footage`, `shorts.find`, `takes.find`) are served read-only: they read the project and its media and never change them. The analysis commands that run models need `--allow-analysis`; edit tools that run one (reframe, shorts, dub, ...) need `--allow-edit`, and the paid ones only estimate here.
* **Validated, previewable, undoable.** Edits go through the command engine: params are checked against the schema, references resolve, and results pass the model invariants and the locked-track guard. `dryRun: true` previews without committing. Every commit (and every `edit_batch`) is one undo step, and `edit_undo` / `edit_redo` work like the menu items.
* **Revisions.** Every result reports the session `revision`. A commit with a stale `expectedRevision` fails with `StaleRevision` instead of editing. Without one, the commit is based on the current revision and the result says `assumedRevision: true`. `idempotencyKey` makes retries safe.
* **Bounded input.** Messages are limited to 4 MiB and 64 levels of nesting, `edit_batch` to 1000 commands, and every argument is checked against its schema.
* **Call timeout.** It is checked at the engine's checkpoints (between batch steps, inside long commands, before a commit). A call that runs past it stops with `TimedOut` and commits nothing. Work between two checkpoints (one model edit) always finishes.
* **Files.** An MCP client is a model steered by what it reads (project content included), so it never picks files: the commands that read or write the files their parameters name are not listed and are refused by name (`PermissionDenied`, `details.touchesFiles`). With `--allow-files` they are served, but every path must be absolute and lie inside the project's folder or a `--files-folder` once symlinks and junctions are resolved (`details.confined` when it does not). `plugins.scan` is never served. The project file itself: `project_save` writes it, or a copy next to it (`copyName` is a plain file name ending in `.wabcut`: no folders, no `..`, no device names). There is no shell or network access.
* **Annotations are hints.** Read tools are `readOnlyHint: true`; edit tools are `destructiveHint: true` (they change the project, although undo restores it); `openWorldHint` is always false.

## Edit results

Edit tools return `{ok, revision, basedOnRevision, dryRun, committed, changes, layout, ...}`:

* `changes`: per sequence, the touched tracks (`"V1"`) with `[start, end)` timecode ranges, plus the added, removed and modified clip ids and what changed on them (`roles`).
* `layout`: the resulting clips of those tracks in the compact `sequence.summary` format (`clipFields` plus arrays). For a dry run this is the preview, so an agent can check the result before committing.
* `createdIds`, `warnings`, `steps` (`edit_batch`), `undone` / `redone`, `canUndo` / `canRedo`, `saved` (autosave), `replayed` (idempotency) when they apply.

## Resources

| URI | Content |
|---|---|
| `wabcut://project/summary` | The `project.summary` JSON plus `revision`. |
| `wabcut://sequence/{id}` | The `sequence.summary` JSON of that sequence plus `revision` (listed per sequence; also a resource template). |

## Tools

Tool names use `_` for the command's `.` (`timeline_rippleDelete` is `timeline.rippleDelete`). Parameters are documented in [docs/commands.md](commands.md); edit tools also take `dryRun`, `expectedRevision` and `idempotencyKey`.

| Tool | Title | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adjustment_add` | New Adjustment Layer | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds an adjustment layer clip (File > New > Adjustment Layer, dropped on the timeline): its effects (colour grade, blur, masks, keyframes) apply to the composite of every video track below it for its duration; its Opacity and blend mode mix the adjusted picture over the unadjusted one. Inside a nested sequence it adjusts that sequence's lower tracks only. "media" reuses an existing adjustment layer item; without it a new one is made for the sequence. Add effects with clip.addEffect. createdIds: the clip (and the new item). |
| `analysis_detectBeats` | Detect Beats | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Finds the tempo and beats of a clip's music: beat markers labelled 1-2-3-4 (downbeats red) and the sequence's beat grid (snapping, edit.snapToBeats and edit.cutToBeats use it). For a media item the beats are listed in media time. Results are cached per source file. |
| `analysis_detectShots` | Detect Shots | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Finds the cuts (hard cuts, fades through black, dissolves; flashes are not cuts) in a clip's video and, for a clip, marks them with sequence markers ("markers": false to only list them). For a media item the cuts are listed in media time. Results are cached per source file. |
| `analysis_speakers` | Who Speaks When | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Active-speaker detection for a multicam source, on this computer: who speaks when (with crosstalk, silence and laughter) and which angle shows whom (close-up or wide), from the transcripts with their speakers, each angle's microphone level and each camera's faces and lip motion. Nothing changes. "angles" sets angles yourself; they win over the guesses. |
| `analysis_subjects` | Find Subjects | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Finds the faces, people and salient regions of a media item over time, shot by shot (5-10 samples a second, denser while the picture moves; faces and people tracked within each shot). Reframing uses it; the result is cached per file, so running it again is cheap. Runs locally: nothing leaves the computer. |
| `audio_addEffect` | Add Track or Master Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds an audio effect to an audio track's stack (applied to the track's mix, before its fader) or to the master bus (applied to the sequence's mix, before the master fader). Parameters not given take their defaults. An audio plugin ("plugin": its effect id from plugins.list) goes in the same way; its parameters are "p<id>" keys. The new instance id is returned in createdIds. |
| `audio_addKeyframe` | Add Track or Master Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a keyframe to a parameter of a track or master effect, or (no "effect") to the fader: "volume" or "pan" - at a timeline time (track and master curves run in timeline time). A constant parameter becomes a curve. |
| `audio_autoDuck` | Auto-Duck Music | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Lowers music under speech: finds speech on the dialogue tracks (transcript words, or the audio level where there is no transcript) and writes volume keyframes on the music tracks' clips - down by "amount" over "attack" before each phrase, back up over "release" after "hold", bridging short pauses. Replaces the music clips' volume keyframes in the range (like Premiere's Auto Ducking); the keys stay editable. "preset": "gameUnderVoice" ducks a gaming recording's game audio and music under the streamer's mic: the tracks named Mic (else the dialogue-role ones) are the speech, the tracks named Game or Desktop Audio (else the effects-role ones) and the music tracks duck, -10 dB with a 0.12 s attack, 0.35 s hold and 0.8 s release; given parameters still win. The report names the tracks used. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `audio_autoTag` | Auto-tag Audio | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Essential Sound's automatic tagging: listens to each audio clip (up to 30 s from its middle) and tags it Dialogue, Music, SFX or Ambience, with a local, deterministic classifier (syllable-rate modulation, pitch glides and held notes, beat regularity, pauses, spectral flatness, crest; nothing leaves the computer). The tag is the clip's Essential Sound record: the panel shows the type and offers its presets; no effect is added. Clips that already have a type keep it unless "overwrite". Without "clips" or "tracks": every audio clip of the sequence. dryRun previews the proposals with their confidence; applying them is one undo step. |
| `audio_bleepProfanity` | Bleep Profanity | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Bleeps (a 1 kHz tone) or mutes the profane words the sequence's transcript finds, in the sound: one audio redaction per media item over those words (with "padding" each side), so they stay bleeped in every use of the media, in preview and export, and captions over them read [bleep]. The picture is untouched. Built-in English and Thai lists, "profanityWords" added, "allowedWords" taken out. dryRun lists the words first. One undo step. |
| `audio_channelLevels` | Measure Channel Levels | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Peak and RMS of each source channel of audio clips (the clip's source range, at most 120 s), and the channels 30 dB or more under the loudest ("silentChannels"): which microphone is on which channel, and whether a recording has sound on one side only. Decodes media; changes nothing. |
| `audio_channels` | Audio Channels | read | What each audio clip plays (its source channel count and channel map: the clip's, its media item's or none), each audio track's channel format and 5.1 panner, and the master's format. A read: it changes nothing. |
| `audio_effects` | Audio Effect Stack | read | The effect stack of an audio track or of the master audio bus: instance ids, effect ids, enabled, parameter values (constants or keyframes in timeline ticks), and the fader after it: "volume" (dB) and, for tracks, "pan". |
| `audio_enhanceSpeech` | Enhance Speech | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Studio-quality dialogue (Premiere's Enhance Speech, Resolve's Voice Isolation): renders each clip's media with DeepFilterNet3 on this computer (no audio leaves it; the model downloads on first use), records the enhanced take on the media item and puts the Enhance Speech effect first in each clip's stack: the clip plays the take blended with the original by "strength" (toggle the effect to compare), before its level and redactions. A take already rendered for the same file and model is reused. Video clips stand for their linked audio. With "render": false only the effect is applied (it plays the original until the take is rendered). Records the take on the media item, so it is a project edit. One undo step. |
| `audio_essentialSound` | Essential Sound | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Essential Sound panel: tags clips as dialogue, music, sfx or ambience and applies a preset of that type as ordinary, editable effects at the top of each clip's stack (an Essential Sound record with the type and options, then one marked effect per setting: Gain for loudness; Dialogue Repair: Reduce Rumble (high-pass), DeHum, Reduce Noise or Enhance Speech, Noise Gate, Reduce Reverb (expander), DeEss; Clarity: EQ preset (podcastVoice, phone, radio, streamerVoice), Dynamics (compressor) and a true-peak limiter last; Creative: reverb (smallRoom, largeRoom, hall, plate, outside); Stereo Width), then matches each clip's loudness to the type's target. Music and ambience can duck under the dialogue (volume keyframes) and music can be remixed to a duration ("duration"); sound effects take a position ("pan"). Applying again replaces what Essential Sound put there; "type": "none" removes it. Presets - dialogue: default, streamerVoice (a gaming mic at -16 LUFS: rumble cut, Reduce Noise, gate, de-esser, EQ, compressor with makeup, limiter at -1 dBTP), cleanUpNoisy, podcastVoice, phone, radio, reduceRoomEcho, removeHum, smallRoom, largeRoom, outside; music: default, background (ducked), wide; sfx: default, background; ambience: default, underDialogue (ducked), wide. "options" change a preset's settings. "tracks" applies it to every clip of those tracks (the mic track of a recording in one request). Without "type" a clip keeps its recorded type, else its track's role. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `audio_fillChannel` | Fill Channel | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Fill Left with Right and Fill Right with Left: both sides of the clips play one channel - for audio heard on one side only ("fix the left-only audio": from left). "from" is the side that has the sound. One undo step. |
| `audio_loudness` | Measure Loudness | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770 loudness as it renders: integrated LUFS, loudness range (LU), true peak (dBTP), sample peak, loudest momentary and short-term LUFS. Targets: the mix (with mute/solo and the master effects: what export writes), a track (its clips and track effects) or a clip on its own. |
| `audio_masterLimiter` | Master True-Peak Limiter | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Puts a true-peak brick-wall limiter at the end of the master audio bus (or updates the one there): no true peak of the mix goes above the ceiling (default -1 dBTP, the streaming and EBU R128 maximum). |
| `audio_moveEffect` | Reorder Track or Master Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves an effect to another position in a track or master stack. |
| `audio_moveKeyframe` | Move Track or Master Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves keyframe `index` of a track or master effect parameter or of the fader ("volume" / "pan", no "effect") to another timeline time; fails if another key is there. |
| `audio_normalize` | Normalize Loudness | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets a gain so the loudness hits a delivery target: YouTube / Spotify -14 LUFS, podcasts and Apple Podcasts -16, broadcast EBU R128 -23, ATSC -24, or a custom "lufs". The gain is the first effect of each clip's, the track's or the master's stack (adjusted when it is already there), measured again and refined until within tolerance, so compressors and limiters after it are accounted for. With "limit" the master gets the true-peak limiter at the preset's ceiling first. One undo step. |
| `audio_remix` | Remix Music | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Remix: retimes a music clip to a target length by rearranging its own bars - repeating or skipping sections where the music around the jump sounds alike (beats and bars, then chroma and MFCC self-similarity) - never by stretching it. The intro and the outro are kept. The clip becomes its pieces on its track (the first keeps its id; they share its level and effects) with a short constant-gain crossfade on each join just before a beat; audio.remixRender makes one rendered take instead. The report lists every join with its confidence (0..1). Target: "duration" (seconds), "end" (a timeline time) or "fit": "video" (the end of the last video clip). One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `audio_remixRender` | Render Music Remix | edit (`--allow-edit`) | audio.remix rendered into one file: the remix of the music clip (the same plan: its own bars rearranged, intro and outro kept, crossfaded joins) becomes a new media item derived from the song (a float WAV in the user's cache), and the clip plays it from its start. The report lists the joins like audio.remix's. Adds media, so it is a project edit. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `audio_removeEffect` | Remove Track or Master Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes an effect from a track or master stack. |
| `audio_removeKeyframe` | Remove Track or Master Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes keyframe `index` of a track or master effect parameter or of the fader ("volume" / "pan", no "effect"); the last one leaves a constant. |
| `audio_routing` | Audio Routing | read | Every audio track's output ("mix" or a submix) and sends, and every submix track with its format, output, sends, effect count, mute and solo. A read: it changes nothing. |
| `audio_separateStems` | Separate Stems | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Splits a music or mixed clip's audio into vocals, drums, bass and other with HTDemucs on this computer (no audio leaves it; the model downloads on first use, and the job refuses on a computer with too little free memory). Each stem becomes a new media item, linked to the source by its provenance ("separated from X with htdemucs"), in a bin named after the source. One undo step. |
| `audio_setChannelVolume` | Set Channel Volume | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Channel Volume: the volume of one channel of audio clips (1-based clip channel), dB, a constant, or with "time" a keyframe there (the channel's volume becomes animated). One undo step. |
| `audio_setChannels` | Modify Audio Channels | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Modify > Audio Channels on clips: which source channels feed each of the clip's channels, in a clip format (mono, stereo, 5.1, adaptive), with mutes and per-channel volume. A "preset" (fillLeft, fillRight, swap, sumToMono, mono with "channel", stereo, identity, default) or a "map". Use it when the two microphones of an interview are on the left and right channels of one file, or a recording has sound on one side only. One undo step. |
| `audio_setEffect` | Set Track or Master Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Enables or disables an effect of a track or master stack, or sets constant parameters. |
| `audio_setMediaChannels` | Modify Media Audio Channels | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Modify > Audio Channels on media items: the channel map every audio clip of the item plays unless it has its own (audio.setChannels). The same presets and maps. It changes media items, so it is a project edit. One undo step. |
| `audio_splitToMono` | Split to Mono | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Splits a clip's channels into linked mono clips, one per source channel, on separate audio tracks (the clip keeps channel 1; the others go on the free audio tracks below it, new ones when needed, or on "tracks"): "split the two mics into separate tracks". Each keeps the clip's level and effects. One undo step. |
| `audio_syncClips` | Synchronize by Audio | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Lines recordings of one event up by their audio: a camera's scratch audio and a separate recorder (dual-system sound), or several cameras. Returns each recording's offset to the reference (the one named, else the first clip with a picture), its confidence, the overlap and the clock drift between the devices (ppm, with the speed that would cancel it). "media" entries may be arrays: a camera's recording split into several files, played back to back in the order they were recorded. With clips and "apply" (Premiere's Synchronize), the other clips move to where they line up with the reference, and the external audio (clips without a picture) links to it; one undo step, dryRun previews it. |
| `autozoom_apply` | Auto Zoom | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Zooms a screen recording in where things happen (clicks, typing, where the cursor rests) and back out when nothing does, like Screen Studio: smooth, editable Position and Scale keyframes on the clip (the AI-9 camera optimiser), never showing outside the frame. Activity comes from a cursor sidecar when there is one, else from the frames. A multicam or nested clip is zoomed as one picture from the recording it shows (the active angle), keys on the clip itself. Running it again replaces its keys. One undo step; dryRun with "preview" returns the zoom path. |
| `bin_create` | New Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a bin (in "parent", default the project's root). Returns its id. |
| `bin_createSearch` | Create Search Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Create Search Bin: a bin named "name" in "parent" (default the root) that lists, live, the bins, sequences and media items of the whole project its "search" finds. It holds nothing itself. Returns its id. |
| `bin_move` | Move to Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves bins, media items and sequences into "target" (absent: the project's root). A bin cannot go into itself or one of its sub-bins. |
| `bin_remove` | Delete Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes bins with everything in them (sub-bins, media items, sequences). Refused while media inside is used by a sequence that is not deleted with it. |
| `bin_rename` | Rename Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames a bin (the name may not be empty). |
| `bin_setSearch` | Edit Search Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Replaces the query of a search bin. |
| `brand_get` | Brand Kit | read | The project's brand kit (null when it has none). |
| `brand_set` | Set Brand Kit | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the project's brand kit - named colours, font roles and logos (media of the project) that graphics, templates and caption styles refer to by name - or removes it (null). Everything that refers to it re-themes. |
| `captions_addCue` | Add Caption | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a cue from "start" to "end" (or for "duration"). Refused where it would overlap another cue (unless the track's style allows overlaps). Returns its index. |
| `captions_addTrack` | New Caption Track | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds an empty caption track, styled by a preset (built in: Clean, Bold Box, Podcast, Shorts, Thai-friendly; or one of the project's) and/or style fields. The default look is white text in a dark box at the bottom. |
| `captions_applyPreset` | Apply Caption Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Gives a caption track the style of a preset: built in (Clean, Bold Box, Podcast, Shorts, Thai-friendly) or one of the project's. |
| `captions_checkSpelling` | Check Spelling in Captions | read | Premiere's spell check for captions: the misspelled words of a caption track's cues ("captionTrack", default the first) in its language (or "language"), from the host's spell checker and the user's dictionary: the cue, the word's byte range in the cue's text, the word, what the checker advises ("suggest", "replace" with the first suggestion, or "delete" a repeated word) and up to 8 suggestions. "available" is false when the host cannot check that language (nothing is listed). At most 2000 words. Corrections are captions.updateCue or captions.findReplace edits. |
| `captions_export` | Export Captions | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a caption track of the sequence to a caption file (Premiere's Create Sidecar File): "format" srt, vtt, scc, mcc (CEA-608: rewrapped to 32 columns and 4 rows; "display" pop-on, roll-up or paint-on), stl (EBU N19), ttml, dfxp, smpte-tt or itt; default from the extension of "path". Timecode-based formats start at the sequence's start timecode. Words the soundtrack bleeps are replaced as in exports. Returns what the format could not hold exactly. The project does not change; a dry run writes nothing. |
| `captions_find` | Find in Captions | read | Premiere's Find (the arrows of Find and Replace): every match of "find" in the cues of a caption track ("captionTrack") or of every caption track of the sequence (default), in track order, then cue order, then position: the caption track, cue index, byte range in the cue's text, the cue's start, and the cue text. Plain text; "matchCase" and "wholeWord" as captions.findReplace. At most 1000 matches. |
| `captions_findReplace` | Find and Replace in Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Find and Replace for captions: replaces every match of "find" in the cues of a caption track ("captionTrack") or of every caption track of the sequence (default), in one undo step - or, with "at" (a match captions.find listed: its caption track, cue and start byte), only that match (Premiere's Replace); the result then names the next match after it ("next", or null). Plain text; "matchCase" and "wholeWord" as Premiere's options (without Match Case, Unicode simple case folding; whole word treats letters, digits and marks of every script as word characters). A dry run lists the matches without changing anything. A replacement that would leave a cue empty is refused. |
| `captions_generate` | Generate Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a caption track from the transcript: cues of at most maxLines lines of maxCharsPerLine characters and maxDuration seconds, broken at pauses, speaker changes and sentence ends; Thai lines break between words, never at spaces that are not there. Replaces a caption track when "replace" names one. |
| `captions_generateFromTranscript` | Captions from Transcript | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a caption track from the sequence's transcript (with the project's corrections and speakers): cues of at most maxLines lines of maxCharsPerLine characters and maxDuration, broken at pauses, speaker changes and (optionally) sentence ends, at least "gap" apart. Thai and other unspaced scripts break between words, and where the host provides line-break rules also inside them. Each cue gets the speaker of most of its words (diarization labels without a speaker get one). "replace" regenerates a caption track and keeps its style. |
| `captions_get` | Caption Cues | read | The cues of a caption track (default: the sequence's first) as arrays in cueFields order: start, end, text (its lines joined by newlines). A cue over redacted speech (a bleep or mute) reads "[bleep]" as a whole; redactedCues lists their indices. sequence.summary lists the caption tracks. |
| `captions_hideProfanity` | Hide Profanity in Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Hide profanity on a caption track that exists: every profane word of its cues reads as its first letter and asterisks ("f***"), with the built-in English and Thai lists, "profanityWords" added and "allowedWords" taken out. One undo step. |
| `captions_import` | Import Captions | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Reads a caption file into a new caption track of the sequence (as Premiere imports a caption file): SubRip (.srt), WebVTT (.vtt), Scenarist SCC and MacCaption MCC (CEA-608), EBU N19 (.stl), W3C TTML / DFXP / SMPTE-TT (.xml, .dfxp) or iTunes Timed Text (.itt); the format comes from the content and the extension unless "format" says. Timecode-based files (SCC, MCC, STL, iTT) count from the sequence's start timecode. Cue text is plain: styles, positions and 608 display modes are approximated (the track takes the placement the cues agree on), as the returned report says. Also Premiere's timed transcript text (.txt: "start - end" timecodes, the speaker, the text; a speaker named there becomes the project's speaker of that name), and the same as a Word document (.docx, transcript.export's). "offset" is added to every cue's time; overlapping cues are trimmed to the next cue's start. Untrusted input: at most 16 MiB and 100,000 cues, 4096 bytes a cue. |
| `captions_mergeCues` | Merge Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Joins "count" consecutive cues (default 2) into one, its text re-wrapped to maxLines lines of maxCharsPerLine characters. |
| `captions_presets` | Caption Presets | read | The caption presets: built in, then the project's, each with its style. |
| `captions_pushTrackStyle` | Push to Track Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Push to Track Style: the caption track's current look becomes its track style (a project preset), and every caption track that follows that style, in every sequence, takes it. Refused for a built-in style (save it under a new name with captions.savePreset). |
| `captions_remove` | Delete Caption Track | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a caption track of the sequence. |
| `captions_removeCue` | Delete Caption | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a cue of a caption track. |
| `captions_removePreset` | Delete Caption Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes one of the project's caption presets. |
| `captions_savePreset` | Save Caption Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Saves a named caption style in the project: a caption track's style, with "style" fields applied on top (or the default look). Replaces the project preset of that name (every caption track that follows it as its Track Style takes the new look); built-in names are refused. |
| `captions_setStyle` | Caption Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes how a caption track looks: font, size (fraction of the frame height), fill, outline, shadow, background box, placement (bottom, top or a custom position), alignment, width, karaoke highlight, speaker names. Fields not given keep their values. Preview and burn-in export both use it. |
| `captions_setTrack` | Caption Track Settings | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames a caption track, sets its language or shows/hides it. |
| `captions_setTrackStyle` | Track Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a caption track follow a caption preset (Premiere's Track Style menu): it takes the preset's style, and saving that preset again (captions.savePreset, captions.pushTrackStyle) restyles every track that follows it. "style": "" makes the track follow nothing (it keeps its look). |
| `captions_shiftCues` | Shift Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves the cues that start in [from, to) (default: all of them) by a signed delta, e.g. to resync captions. Refused when a cue would start before 0 or overlap a cue that stays. |
| `captions_splitCue` | Split Caption | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Cuts a cue in two at a time inside it. The text splits at "textOffset" (a byte offset) or else at the line-break opportunity nearest the same share of the text (Thai and other unspaced scripts break between words where the host provides line-break rules). |
| `captions_translate` | Translate Captions | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Translates a caption track into new caption tracks, one per language, keeping the cue timing: cues that would read too fast in the target language borrow time from the gaps, merge with a neighbour or move words across, and text that does not fit two lines is split into more cues (Thai broken between words). The corrections layer applies first, and bleeped words stay "[bleep]" (never sent as content). A local model (OPUS-MT, on this computer) or the user's cloud model (consent and spend cap; caption text only) with a glossary and a tone. One undo step; "estimate" prices a cloud run first. |
| `captions_updateCue` | Edit Caption | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a cue's text, start, end or speaker (null clears the speaker). |
| `captions_updateFromTranscript` | Update Captions from Transcript | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Rewrites the text of a caption track's cues from the transcript words under them (after transcript corrections), keeping their timing and style; cues with no words under them stay as they are. |
| `cdl_export` | Export CDL | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes clips' colour wheels as an ASC CDL: slope = gain - lift, offset = lift + offset, power = gamma, saturation. .cc holds one clip; .ccc and .cdl several (ids are the clip names). Refuses to replace a file unless "overwrite". |
| `cdl_import` | Import CDL | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Sets clips' colour wheels from an ASC CDL file (.cc, .ccc, .cdl): the correction whose id is the clip's name, else the one at the clip's position, or "index". Values beyond the wheels' ranges are clamped (with a warning). |
| `clip_addEffect` | Apply Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds an effect to the stack of each clip (video effects on video clips, audio effects on audio clips). Parameters not given take their defaults. An audio plugin ("plugin": its effect id from plugins.list) goes on audio clips the same way. The new instance ids are returned in createdIds. |
| `clip_addKeyframe` | Add Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a keyframe at a timeline time inside the clip (or replaces the one there). A parameter that was constant becomes animated with just this key. Keyframes stick to the media: slipping the clip moves them with the picture, trims hide but keep them. |
| `clip_details` | Clip Details | read | Everything about one clip: track, timeline and source range (ticks and timecode), media, stream, speed, enabled, label colour, linked clips and all parameter values (and effects' text data, e.g. Simple Text's text). |
| `clip_enable` | Enable | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Enables or disables clips (Premiere Shift+E). Disabled clips stay in place but are not shown or heard. |
| `clip_fade` | Fade | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Fades clips in and/or out with keyframes: opacity on video clips (to 0), level on audio clips (to -144 dB). The fade ends (or starts) at the value the parameter has there. |
| `clip_find` | Find Clips | read | Finds clips by name (case-insensitive substring), by a time they cover, by track and by media. Returns arrays in clipFields order. |
| `clip_frameHold` | Frame Hold | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Holds the frame at a time. Without duration (Add Frame Hold) the clip is cut there and the rest shows that frame; with a duration (Insert Frame Hold Segment) a still of that length is inserted, rippling the track and sync-locked tracks. Effects keep animating through the hold. |
| `clip_frameHoldOptions` | Frame Hold Options | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Video Options > Frame Hold Options: the whole video clip holds one frame - at a source timecode, a sequence timecode, its In point, its Out point or the playhead ("time": a media time for sourceTimecode, a sequence time for sequenceTimecode and playhead) - keeping its place and length. "holdFilters" holds its keyframed effects at that frame too (off: they keep animating). "enabled": false plays the clip normally again from the frame it held. Add Frame Hold / Insert Frame Hold Segment are clip.frameHold. |
| `clip_group` | Group | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Groups clips (Premiere's Clip > Group, Ctrl+G): clicking any of them selects the whole group, so it moves, copies and deletes together; Alt-click selects one clip of it. Clips leave the groups they were in. Unlike a link, clips on any tracks can be grouped. |
| `clip_insert` | Insert | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Insert edit (Premiere ','): puts a media source range onto the patched tracks at a time and pushes later material on those tracks and every sync-locked track later, cutting through clips there. Video and audio clips are linked. |
| `clip_instantReplay` | Instant Replay | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Replays a moment right after itself in slow motion, Premiere-style instant replay in one step: the moment's clips are copied and inserted right after it (everything later moves, sync-locked tracks stay in sync) with a speed ramp (100 % easing into "speed" and back), the REPLAY stinger template over the replay and a white flash at each cut. The moment is a video clip ("clip": its span, and its linked clips), or a range ("in"/"out", default the sequence In/Out marks: every clip of media overlapping it). Graphics and titles are not replayed. The replay is silent unless "includeAudio" (slowed, the pitch drops). One undo step. |
| `clip_link` | Link | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Links clips so they select and edit together. |
| `clip_move` | Move | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves clips in time and across tracks. "overwrite" (plain drag) replaces what is at the destination; "insert" (Ctrl-drag) makes room there; "rearrange" (Ctrl+Alt-drag) closes the clips' old place and makes room at the drop, on the dragged clips' and the destination tracks only (a clip dropped at the cut after its neighbour swaps with it). With copy (Alt-drag) the clips are copied there instead and the originals stay (overwrite or insert; not rearrange). Clips cannot start before 0. |
| `clip_moveEffect` | Reorder Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves an effect to another position in the clip's stack. |
| `clip_moveKeyframe` | Move Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves a keyframe to another timeline time inside the clip. |
| `clip_openNested` | Open Nested Sequence | read | The sequence a nested or multicam clip plays (open it to edit inside), the range of it the clip shows and, for a multicam clip, its active angles. |
| `clip_overwrite` | Overwrite | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Overwrite edit (Premiere '.'): puts a media source range onto the patched tracks at a time, replacing whatever is there. Nothing moves. |
| `clip_pasteAttributes` | Paste Attributes | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Paste Attributes (Ctrl+Alt+V): the chosen attributes of the clipboard's clip (the first one of each target's kind: video attributes from the copied video clip, audio ones from the audio clip) or of "source" onto "clips". Parameter values and keyframes replace the target's; effects are added after its own; time remapping replaces its speed. Keyframes keep their time from the clip's start, or stretch to the target's length with "scaleTimes". One undo step; "changes" lists what each clip took and skipped (dryRun previews). |
| `clip_removeAttributes` | Remove Attributes | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Remove Attributes: the chosen parameters go back to their defaults (keyframes too), time remapping is turned off (the clip plays at 100 % from the frame it started on), effects are removed by id (or all). One undo step; "changes" lists what each clip lost. |
| `clip_removeEffect` | Remove Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes an effect instance from a clip's stack. |
| `clip_removeKeyframe` | Remove Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a keyframe; removing the last one leaves the parameter constant at its value. |
| `clip_rename` | Rename Clip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames clips (the name shown on the timeline; the media keeps its name). |
| `clip_replace` | Replace With Clip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Replace Edit (Sequence > Replace With Clip; Shift-drag from the Source Monitor, Alt-drag from the Project panel onto a clip): the clips (with linked partners) play "media" instead - same place, length, speed and direction, effects and attributes kept; the clip takes the item's name. From Source Monitor / From Bin: the first clip starts with the item's In mark (or "sourceIn"); "matchFrame" (From Source Monitor, Match Frame) lines the Source Monitor's frame up with the sequence playhead instead. Linked partners keep their sync. Refused when the item lacks the media the clip needs. |
| `clip_rippleTrim` | Ripple Edit | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ripple edit (B): moves a clip's In or Out point and ripples later material (sync-locked tracks too). |
| `clip_roll` | Rolling Edit | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Rolling edit (N): moves the edit point at a clip's edge, trimming the neighbour the other way. |
| `clip_scaleToFrameSize` | Scale to Frame Size | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Video Options > Scale to Frame Size (also the clip's right-click menu): fits each video clip's picture into the sequence frame (whole picture visible, letterboxed when the aspect differs) before its Motion, so Motion > Scale stays 100 % and a later Scale applies to the fitted picture. "enabled": false turns it off (the picture shows at its pixel size again). Audio clips in the list (or linked) are skipped. |
| `clip_setAnimated` | Toggle Animation | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's stopwatch. On: the constant value becomes one keyframe at "time" (default: the clip's start). Off: all keyframes are deleted and the parameter keeps the value it has at "time". |
| `clip_setBlendMode` | Set Blend Mode | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the blend mode of video clips (the Opacity section's Blend Mode, Premiere's list): how each clip combines with what is below it. "normal" puts it over; the darken, lighten, contrast, inversion and component groups follow Premiere's menu. Opacity (keyframable) still applies on top. Audio clips are refused. |
| `clip_setColor` | Set Label Color | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the label colour of clips (0-15). |
| `clip_setEffect` | Set Effect | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Turns an effect on or off or sets its parameters (constants; animate them with clip.addKeyframe and "effect") or its text data ("data": Simple Text's {"text": "..."}, Image Matte Key's {"image": "media:<id>"} naming a still image in the project; an empty string removes it). |
| `clip_setFade` | Set Fade | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets a clip's fade in (edge "head") or fade out ("tail"), what dragging the fade handle at a clip's top corner does: a one-sided transition inside the clip, Cross Dissolve on video (from or to black) and Constant Power on audio (from or to silence). The duration is clamped to the clip; 0 removes the fade. An edge that already has a transition with the neighbouring clip is refused. (clip.fade keyframes opacity or volume instead.) |
| `clip_setFieldOptions` | Field Options | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Video Options > Field Options for interlaced footage. "reverseFieldDominance" swaps the clip's field order; "processing" is "none" (default), "interlaceConsecutiveFrames" (kept for interchange: Wabcut renders progressive frames), "alwaysDeinterlace" (show one field, the dominant one, even in an interlaced sequence or on footage without fields) or "flickerRemoval" (blend the fields slightly against flicker on thin horizontal lines). Interlaced footage in a progressive sequence is deinterlaced anyway, both fields shown when the sequence runs at the field rate. Audio clips in the list (or linked) are skipped. One undo step. |
| `clip_setKeyframe` | Set Keyframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a keyframe's value, interpolation (hold, linear, bezier, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut) or Bezier handles (slope in units per second, influence 0..1 of the segment). |
| `clip_setMotion` | Motion | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets a video clip's Motion - Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point - in one step, as dragging the clip in the Program Monitor does (move, scale by a handle, rotate outside a corner, move the anchor point). Each value given is in the model's unit: position and anchor in pixels from the centre (sequence pixels for position, source pixels for the anchor), scale as a factor (1 = 100%), rotation in degrees clockwise. A parameter whose stopwatch is on gets a keyframe at "time" (the key there changes, else a new one continues the curve's shape); a constant one takes the value. Parameters left out keep their values. |
| `clip_setParam` | Set Clip Parameter | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets one effect parameter (motion, opacity, volume, pan) on clips. |
| `clip_setTimeInterpolation` | Time Interpolation | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Clip > Video Options > Time Interpolation: how retimed video clips make the frames between their media's frames (a speed other than 100 %, reverse, time remapping, Rate Stretch, or footage at another frame rate than the sequence's). "frameSampling" (the default) repeats or drops whole frames; "frameBlending" mixes the two frames around each moment; "opticalFlow" warps both along their motion and blends them (smoothest; the render bar shows those sections red until rendered). Linked audio partners are left alone. |
| `clip_setToFillFrame` | Set to Fill Frame | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Fill Frame (the clip's right-click menu): sets each video clip's Motion > Scale so its picture covers the whole sequence frame, cropping what overhangs (a 16:9 clip in a 9:16 Short fills the height). Keys on Scale are replaced by the constant; Scale to Frame Size goes off. data.scale: the first clip's new Scale in percent. |
| `clip_setToFrameSize` | Set to Frame Size | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Set to Frame Size (Fit to Frame Size in Premiere 25 and later; Clip > Video Options and the right-click menu): sets each video clip's Motion > Scale so its whole picture fits the sequence frame, so the Effect Controls show how much it was scaled. Keys on Scale are replaced by the constant; Scale to Frame Size goes off. data.scale: the first clip's new Scale in percent. |
| `clip_shake` | Camera Shake | edit (`--allow-edit`) | A camera shake on a video clip from "at": Motion Position (and Rotation) keys of a seeded random pattern that decays over "seconds", plus a slight zoom so the clip's edges do not show ("cover"). The same request makes the same shake ("seed" picks another). Keys already inside the shake are replaced. One undo step. |
| `clip_slide` | Slide | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Slide (U): moves a clip between its neighbours, trimming them to compensate. |
| `clip_slip` | Slip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Slip (Y): shifts which source frames clips show, keeping their place and length. |
| `clip_speedDuration` | Speed/Duration | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ctrl+R: plays each clip's material at a new speed (percent; 200 = twice as fast) or fits it into a new duration; can reverse it and keep audio pitch. With ripple, later material on the track and sync-locked tracks moves; without, the clip only grows into the gap after it. |
| `clip_splitAtShots` | Split at Shots | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Razors each clip at the cuts in its video (scene-edit detection), with its linked partners. One undo step; dryRun previews the split. |
| `clip_trim` | Trim | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Trim an edge (selection tool): moves a clip's In or Out point without moving anything else. Clamped to neighbours, source media and one frame; the delta actually applied is returned. |
| `clip_ungroup` | Ungroup | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ungroups clips (Premiere's Clip > Ungroup, Ctrl+Shift+G): every group one of the clips belongs to is dissolved, all its members included. Clips that are not grouped are left alone. |
| `clip_unlink` | Unlink | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Takes clips out of their link groups. |
| `clip_zoomPunch` | Zoom Punch | edit (`--allow-edit`) | A punch-in zoom on a moment of a video clip: Motion Scale keys ease in to "scale" times the clip's scale, hitting at "at", hold, and ease back out ("attack" and "release" are shares of "seconds"). With "focus" the zoom closes in on that point of the frame (Position keys too). Keys already inside the punch are replaced. One undo step; the keys stay editable. |
| `clipboard_copy` | Copy | read | Copies clips (with their link partners unless "linked": false) to the clipboard exactly: speed, reverse, freeze frames, time remapping, effects and keyframes, names, labels, links, the transitions between them and the markers over them (captions on request). The project does not change. |
| `clipboard_cut` | Cut | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Copies clips to the clipboard (like clipboard.copy) and deletes them, leaving gaps (Premiere's Cut). One undo step. |
| `clipboard_get` | Clipboard | read | What the clipboard holds: clips, length, tracks, markers, captions, media; with "export" also the clipboard as JSON text. |
| `clipboard_paste` | Paste | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Pastes the clipboard (or a "document" from clipboard.copy's export) at "at": overwrite (Ctrl+V) replaces what lies under the pasted clips, insert (Ctrl+Shift+V) first opens the clipboard's length on the destination and sync-locked tracks. Clips go to the lowest targeted track of their kind (or "videoTrack" / "audioTrack") plus their copied offsets; missing tracks are added. Media is the project's own when it has the file (by id, fingerprint or path), else it is added; "notes" say which. One undo step. |
| `color_auto` | Auto Color | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Auto colour: looks at the clip (at "time", default its middle) without its grade and sets the grade's white balance (temperature, tint) and levels (exposure, whites, blacks) as ordinary, editable Basic parameters. One undo step. |
| `color_grade_copy` | Apply Grade | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Copies a clip's whole colour grade (every parameter with its keyframes, curves, LUTs, stage switches and the on / off state) over other clips' grades: "clips", or with "scope": "media" every other video clip that shows the same source (the same media item; for nested clips the same sequence, and for multicam the same angle). Each target's first grade is replaced in place (its id, stack position and its own masks stay); a target without a grade gets one at the end of its stack. "replace": false appends a second grade instead, as Paste Attributes does. Audio clips, clips on locked tracks and the source itself are skipped (listed with the reason). One undo step; refused when the source has no grade or no target changes. |
| `color_grade_get` | Get Color Grade | read | A clip's grade at a time (default: its middle): parameters (only those changed unless "all"), animated ones, curves, LUTs, missing LUTs and whether it does anything. "grade": null when the clip has none. |
| `color_grade_set` | Set Color Grade | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets a clip's colour grade (wabcut.color.grade; added at the end of the stack when the clip has none): "params" by registry key (only those given change; effect.list lists them with ranges), "stages" on or off (basic, creative, curves, wheels, hsl, vignette), "curves" as [x, y] points (master/red/green/blue x and y in 0..1; hueSat/hueHue/hueLuma x = hue in turns and lumaSat/satSat y with 0.5 = no change; [] resets), and the "inputLut" / "look" ("builtin:<name>" or "asset:<id>" from lut.list; "" removes). A constant replaces an animated parameter. One undo step for every clip. |
| `color_inputSpace_get` | Get Input Colour Space | read | Video clips' input colour spaces: the override (null = auto), what auto reads (the stream's tags or the detected camera log), the log the media's metadata names (null = none), and the one in effect, with the project's colour management. Read only. |
| `color_inputSpace_set` | Set Input Colour Space | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets how video clips' pictures are read into the working space (Premiere Pro's Override Media Color Space): "auto" follows the stream's colour tags (BT.709, BT.2020, PQ, HLG, sRGB, linear) and the camera log the media's metadata names, or a space by id - camera log formats are chosen here when the metadata does not say (s-log3, s-log3-cine, v-log, logc3, logc4, canon-log3, canon-log2, red-log3g10, apple-log, acescct; color.management.get lists them all). Direct Rec.709 tone-maps log and HDR clips into SDR. One undo step for every clip. |
| `color_management_get` | Get Colour Management | read | The project's colour management, Premiere Pro's sequence Color Setup: "mode" (rec709 = Direct Rec.709 (SDR), the default; hdr-hlg = Direct HLG (HDR); hdr-pq = Direct PQ (HDR); aces = Wide Gamut (Tone Mapped), ACES 1.3 with the grade in ACEScct; wide-gamut = Wide Gamut (No Tone Mapping); off = Disable Color Management), the HDR peak and graphics (reference) white in nits, whether log media is auto-detected, and the modes and input colour spaces there are (ids, names and descriptions, for color.management.set and color.inputSpace.set). |
| `color_management_set` | Set Colour Management | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the project's colour management (Premiere Pro's sequence Color Setup): "mode" rec709 (Direct Rec.709 (SDR), the default: SDR media as it is, HDR media and log clips tone-mapped into SDR on input), hdr-hlg or hdr-pq (Direct HLG / PQ (HDR): a linear Rec.2020 working space, SDR clips and titles at the graphics white; the monitor shows a tone-mapped SDR preview, HDR exports carry HLG or PQ), aces (Wide Gamut (Tone Mapped): ACES 1.3, clips read through their input colour space into ACEScg, the grade works in ACEScct, the ACES output transforms), wide-gamut (Wide Gamut (No Tone Mapping): ACEScg, clipped at the output's white) or off (Disable Color Management: no conversion at all). "peakNits" (100..10000, default 1000) is the HDR mastering peak, "referenceWhiteNits" (80..400, default 203) the graphics white where SDR white lands, "autoDetectLog" (default true) reads clips as the camera log their metadata names. Only the given fields change. One undo step. |
| `color_match` | Color Match | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes clips look like a reference frame: "reference" is {"clip", "time"} (that clip as it looks, alone) or a sequence time (the whole picture). Fits the grade's exposure, contrast, temperature, tint and saturation so the clip's colour statistics (Oklab mean and spread) move to the reference's, by "strength"; "skinPriority" weighs skin tones more, "faceDetection" (Premiere's Face Detection) the faces' skin. Editable parameters, one undo step. |
| `color_matchScene` | Match Scene | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Shot-to-shot consistency: matches every clip of the reference clip's scene to it - "scene" (default) is the run of clips on its track cut from the same take without gaps (what clip.splitAtShots makes), "track" every clip on its track, "media" every clip of the same media item, or an explicit "clips" list. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `dub_create` | Dub | edit (`--allow-edit`) | AI voice-over in another language with the user's own voice provider (ElevenLabs, OpenAI or Gemini; BYOK): each caption cue is spoken and fitted to its slot (sped up at most 15 %, pitch kept; else moved and flagged), on a new "Dub" audio track with the Dialogue role, the original dialogue ducked under it, as one undo step. Bleeped words are never spoken. The audio is marked AI-generated. Paid: "estimate" prices it; a run needs "maxCost" and the app's approval (standalone CLI/MCP and the assistant only estimate or open the Dub dialog). |
| `edit_clear` | Delete | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Delete (Premiere Delete key): removes clips and leaves gaps. |
| `edit_cutToBeats` | Cut to Beats | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Music-video assembly: places the given clips' media (from each clip's source In) and media items (from their start) one after another, each lasting beatsPerCut beats of the beat grid, starting at the first beat at or after "at" (the playhead). Overwrites what is there; video goes to videoTrack, audio only when audioTrack is given (the music usually stays alone). |
| `edit_insertFromSource` | Insert from Source | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Insert edit from the source (Premiere ','), with three-point editing: the source marks (stored on the media unless given), the sequence In/Out marks and the playhead decide where it goes and what it uses. Later material on the patched and sync-locked tracks moves later. A four-point edit whose ranges differ takes a "fit" choice (Premiere's Fit Clip dialog). |
| `edit_overwriteFromSource` | Overwrite from Source | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Overwrite edit from the source (Premiere '.'), with three-point editing like edit.insertFromSource: replaces what is on the patched tracks; nothing moves. "fit": "speed" retimes the clip to fill the sequence In/Out exactly. |
| `edit_snapToBeats` | Snap to Beats | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Trims each clip's head and/or tail to the nearest beat of the beat grid when it is within the tolerance (linked partners follow). Edges that cannot reach their beat (a neighbouring clip, too little media) are left and reported. |
| `effect_analyzeRollingShutter` | Analyze Rolling Shutter | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Rolling Shutter Repair's analysis: measures the picture's motion per frame of a video clip's footage and keys it (motion.x, motion.y: source pixels per frame) into the clip's Rolling Shutter Repair (added at the top of its stack when it has none), which then skews each line back by its share of the scan (Rolling Shutter Rate, Scan Direction). Shares the cached analysis with Warp Stabilizer's Position method. |
| `effect_analyzeStabilization` | Analyze Stabilization | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Warp Stabilizer's Analyze: tracks the camera motion of a video clip's footage, smooths the camera path with the effect's settings (Result, Smoothness, Method, Preserve Scale, Framing, Maximum Scale, Action-Safe Margin, Additional Scale, Detailed Analysis, Rolling Shutter Ripple, Crop Less Smooth More) and keys the compensating transform per frame into the clip's Warp Stabilizer (added at the top of its stack when it has none), with the crop or auto-scale that hides the moving borders. The keys stay editable. Changing a setting and running it again re-smooths from the cached analysis. Runs as a job with progress and cancel; a dry run analyses and previews the keys. |
| `effect_list` | List Effects | read | The effects and transitions Wabcut knows: id, name, category, kind (video, audio, videoTransition, audioTransition) and parameters as arrays in paramFields order. builtIn effects are part of every clip (set their parameters with clip.setParam or keyframes); the others go into a clip's stack. |
| `effects_addToCustomBin` | Add to Custom Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Puts effects, transitions or presets in a custom bin (dragging them there in Premiere). Items already in it stay once. |
| `effects_applyPreset` | Apply Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Applies a preset to clips (double-click or drag from the Effects panel's Presets bin): its stack effects are added after each clip's own, its fixed effects replace the clip's Motion / Opacity / Volume / Panner values (keyframes included), and keyframes are timed by its type. Clips of the other kind (a video preset on audio) are skipped and reported. Built-in presets (effects.library) and the user's. |
| `effects_deleteCustomItem` | Delete Custom Item | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a user item of the Effects panel (Premiere's Delete Custom Item): a preset (it leaves custom bins and favourites too), a presets bin with the presets in it, a custom bin, or one item of a custom bin ("customBin" with "item"). Built-in presets and bins cannot be deleted. |
| `effects_exportPresets` | Export Effect Presets | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes presets to a file (Premiere's Export Preset) another Wabcut can import: named presets (built-in or the user's) and/or the user's presets in a presets bin ("" = all of them). |
| `effects_importPresets` | Import Presets | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Adds the presets of a presets file (effects.exportPresets) to the user's library (Premiere's Import Presets). The file is untrusted: read bounded and checked. A name in use gets a number ("Glow 2"). |
| `effects_library` | Effects Library | read | The Effects panel's presets and the user's items: every preset (the built-in Presets and Lumetri Presets bins, and the user's presets with their presets bins; name, type, description, bin, kind, effects), the user's presets bins, custom bins (their items: effects, transitions and presets) and favourites. Built-in presets are made for the sequence's frame size (PiP positions). The library is the user's, kept by the host ("file"; "error" when it could not be read or written). |
| `effects_newCustomBin` | New Custom Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a custom bin in the Effects panel (Premiere's New Custom Bin): a bin of shortcuts to effects, transitions and presets. Default name: "Custom Bin 01", "Custom Bin 02", ... |
| `effects_newPresetsBin` | New Presets Bin | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a bin in the Presets bin for the user's presets ("A/B": B inside A; the parents are made too). |
| `effects_renameCustomItem` | Rename Custom Item | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames a custom bin, a presets bin or a user preset (custom bins and favourites follow a renamed preset). |
| `effects_savePreset` | Save Effect Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Saves effects of a clip as a preset in the user's library (Premiere's Effect Controls > Save Preset): stack effects by index and the clip's fixed effects (motion, opacity with its blend mode, volume, panner), with their keyframes and the preset type that times them on other clips. LUT files are referred to by path, tracked matte masks are left out ("notes"). Not an undo step: the library is the user's. |
| `effects_setFavorite` | Add to Favorites | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Marks an effect, transition or preset as a favourite (the Effects panel's Favorites bin), or with "favorite": false takes it off the list. |
| `effects_setPresetProperties` | Preset Properties | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a user preset (Premiere's Preset Properties): its name (custom bins and favourites follow), type, description, or the presets bin it is in. |
| `export_describe` | Describe Export | read | What an export of the sequence with a preset (and overrides) would write, without exporting: the output file, the resolved settings (container, codecs, size, frame rate, effects, metadata, ...), the range and its frame count. |
| `export_preset_delete` | Delete Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a user preset (built-in presets cannot be deleted). |
| `export_preset_export` | Export Preset | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a preset (built-in or the user's) to a preset file others can import. |
| `export_preset_import` | Import Preset | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Import Preset: reads a Wabcut export preset file (.json) and stores it with the user's presets. The file is checked like any untrusted input (types, ranges, sizes). |
| `export_preset_save` | Save Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Save Preset: stores a preset's settings with overrides on top as a user preset (a JSON file in the user's export presets folder). "overwrite" replaces one of the same name. |
| `export_presets` | Export Presets | read | The export presets: the built-in ones (YouTube, Shorts / TikTok / Reels, Twitch, Discord sizes, ProRes / DNxHR / DNxHD masters, ProRes 4444 / QuickTime Animation / CineForm with alpha, MP3 / AAC / AIFF / WAV audio, PNG / TIFF / DPX / JPEG / Targa / OpenEXR image sequences, HDR) and the user's saved ones: id, name, description, builtIn, and the full settings. |
| `export_queue` | Send to Media Encoder | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Queues exports of the sequence, one per preset in "presets" (to the matching "outputs"), with the same overrides: Premiere's Export with several destinations and Send to Media Encoder. They run one after another in the background. With "hold" they wait in the queue until export.queue.start (Media Encoder's queue before Start Queue). |
| `export_queue_cancel` | Stop | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Cancels jobs (a running export leaves no file). "jobs": the job ids; "all": every job of the queue. |
| `export_queue_list` | Export Queue | read | The export queue: every job with its output, preset, state (held, queued, running, paused, done, failed, cancelled), progress 0..1 and detail (the result or the error). |
| `export_queue_pause` | Pause | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Pauses jobs: a running one between two frames, a queued one is held. "jobs": the job ids; "all": every job of the queue. |
| `export_queue_remove` | Remove | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes finished jobs from the list. "jobs": the job ids; "all": every job of the queue. |
| `export_queue_resume` | Resume | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Resumes paused jobs and starts held ones. "jobs": the job ids; "all": every job of the queue. |
| `export_queue_start` | Start Queue | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Starts held jobs (Media Encoder's Start Queue). "jobs": the job ids; "all": every job of the queue. |
| `export_quick` | Quick Export | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Quick Export: exports the sequence with one preset (default "match-source") to "output" (default: next to the project, named after the sequence) in the background, through the export queue. Returns the job and what it writes; export.queue.list follows it. |
| `export_watchFolder_add` | Add Watch Folder | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Watches a folder: every media file dropped into it (once it stops growing) is exported with the preset into "output" (default "<folder>/Output"), through the export queue; with "moveSources" (default true) the source then moves into "<folder>/Source". |
| `export_watchFolder_list` | Watch Folders | read | Media Encoder's Watch Folders: each folder, its preset and output folder, whether sources move into "Source" once encoded, and how many files are queued, done and failed. |
| `export_watchFolder_remove` | Remove Watch Folder | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Stops watching a folder (its queued exports go on). |
| `freeform_alignToGrid` | Align to Grid | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Align to Grid: the named items (all when none) snapped to the nearest grid cell of the view's clip size; items on one cell stack. |
| `freeform_get` | Freeform View | read | A bin's Freeform view: its clip size, where each item is (back to front) and its saved layouts. |
| `freeform_removeLayout` | Delete Layout | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes the bin's saved Freeform layout "name". |
| `freeform_resetToGrid` | Reset to Grid | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Reset to Grid: every item of the bin placed row by row in the chosen order ("by": name, label or type; bins, sequences and media keep their groups), "columns" per row, at size 1. |
| `freeform_restoreLayout` | Restore Layout | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Arranges the bin's Freeform view as saved layout "name". |
| `freeform_saveLayout` | Save as New Layout | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Saves the bin's Freeform arrangement under "name" (replacing a layout of that name). |
| `freeform_set` | Arrange in Freeform View | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Places items of a bin in its Freeform view (Premiere's Freeform view: thumbnails anywhere, overlapping ones stacked; later items over earlier ones). "items" replaces the arrangement unless "merge" (default true) keeps the other items where they are, moving the named ones to the front. "scale" is the clip size. |
| `gen_broll` | Generate broll | edit (`--allow-edit`) | App: opens a human-reviewed Generate proposal with consent and cost preview; acceptance imports one staged edit. Standalone CLI/MCP refuses paid generation without an approval host. |
| `gen_extend` | Generate extend | edit (`--allow-edit`) | App: opens a human-reviewed Generate proposal with consent and cost preview; acceptance imports one staged edit. Standalone CLI/MCP refuses paid generation without an approval host. |
| `gen_image` | Generate image | edit (`--allow-edit`) | App: opens a human-reviewed Generate proposal with consent and cost preview; acceptance imports one staged edit. Standalone CLI/MCP refuses paid generation without an approval host. |
| `gen_sfx` | Generate sfx | edit (`--allow-edit`) | App: opens a human-reviewed Generate proposal with consent and cost preview; acceptance imports one staged edit. Standalone CLI/MCP refuses paid generation without an approval host. |
| `graphic_add` | New Graphic | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a motion graphic as a clip on a video track (overwriting what is there): "graphic" is the graphic's JSON (docs/graphics.md: name, width/height of its design canvas - default the sequence's frame - layers of text, shapes, images and groups, responsive time). Layer ids 0 get fresh ones. Add layers later with graphic.addLayer, animate them with graphic.applyPreset or keyframes in the layer JSON. createdIds: the clip, and the canvas media item when the project had none of this size. |
| `graphic_addLayer` | Add Graphic Layer | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a layer (JSON, docs/graphics.md) to a graphic clip: on top of "parent" (a group layer; default the top level), or at "index" (0 = bottom). An id of 0 or one in use gets a fresh one; returns it as "layer". |
| `graphic_align` | Align Layers | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Essential Graphics Align and Distribute: lines layers up with the video frame ("to": "frame", the default) or with each other ("selection") - left, horizontal centre, right, top, vertical centre, bottom - or spaces three or more evenly (distributeHorizontal / distributeVertical: centres evenly spaced between the outermost two). Layers move by their Position (an animated one with all its keys), measured as drawn at "time" (default the clip's start). |
| `graphic_applyPreset` | Apply Animation Preset | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Animates a layer with editable keyframes: fade, slide, scalePop, bounce (the transform), typewriter and wordByWord (a text-range animator: characters or words appear in turn), wipe (a mask). "in" animates the graphic's start, "out" its end, "loop" repeats over the whole clip. Keys inside the preset's time replace the ones there; others stay. |
| `graphic_checkSpelling` | Check Spelling in Graphic | read | Spell check for a graphic clip's text: the misspelled words of every text layer (groups included, bottom to top), each in its layer's language (or "language"), from the host's spell checker and the user's dictionary - the layer, the word's byte range in the layer's text, the word, the checker's advice and up to 8 suggestions, as captions.checkSpelling lists them. Corrections are graphic.setText edits. |
| `graphic_get` | Graphic | read | A graphic clip's graphic as JSON (docs/graphics.md), with its layers listed flat (bottom to top, groups before their children) and, for a template instance, its template and field values. |
| `graphic_removeLayer` | Delete Graphic Layer | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a layer from a graphic clip (a group with its children); pins to it and template fields bound to it go too. |
| `graphic_resolve` | Graphic Draw List | read | The draw list of a graphic clip at a timeline time (default its start): every visible layer bottom to top with its transform to canvas pixels [a, b, c, d, e, f], opacity, blend mode, shadow, masks, and its path and paints, text runs (and per-character animator values) or image - with the brand kit applied. What the renderer draws (docs/graphics.md). |
| `graphic_setRoll` | Roll/Crawl Options | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a graphic clip roll up (credits: Premiere's Essential Graphics Roll) or crawl left or right (a ticker: the Legacy Titler's Crawl Left / Crawl Right) over the clip, so the clip's length sets the speed; "roll": null stops it. Start Off Screen / End Off Screen (default on), Preroll and Postroll (held at the start / end), Ease-In and Ease-Out (speeding up / slowing down) as Premiere has them. The graphic is designed in place: layers below the frame are the rest of the roll. |
| `graphic_setTextPath` | Type on a Path | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Puts a text layer on a path (the Legacy Titler's Path Type tool, After Effects' Path Options): "shape" line, arc (the top of an ellipse: text over a rainbow), circle (clockwise from its left: text round the outside) or wave, "width" and "height" in pixels, centred on the layer's origin - or custom "vertices" ("closed" for a closed path); "none" puts it back on straight lines. Options: "reverse" (Reverse Path), "perpendicular" (characters turn with the path, default true), "forceAlignment" (spread from the first margin to the last), "firstMargin" / "lastMargin" (pixels; keyframe the first margin with graphic.updateLayer to send the text along the path). Without "shape" only the options change. The text's alignment places it between the margins. One undo step. |
| `graphic_update` | Edit Graphic | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a graphic clip's graphic with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) over its JSON (graphic.get): objects merge, null resets a key to its default, arrays ("layers") are replaced whole. For one layer use graphic.updateLayer. |
| `graphic_updateLayer` | Edit Graphic Layer | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a layer of a graphic clip with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) over the layer's JSON: {"text": {"runs": [{"text": "New"}]}} replaces the runs, {"transform": {"x": 200}} moves it, a curve ({"keys": [{"t": ticks, "v": value}, ...]} or just the array of keys) animates it. Its id stays. |
| `highlights_find` | Find Highlights | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Finds the best moments of a gaming recording on this computer: game-audio spikes, the player's voice (louder or higher than usual, shouting, laughter), the picture (fast action, flashes, bursts of picture changes), the recording's imported Twitch / YouTube chat log (busy chat, emotes; highlights.importChat) and OBS chapter markers or a marker file next to the recording. Each moment gets a score, a confidence and the reasons, and a marker ("Highlight 1: ..."; earlier highlight markers are replaced). For a media item the moments are in media time and become clip markers. Measurements are cached per source file. |
| `highlights_importChat` | Import Chat Log | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Reads a stream's chat log (TwitchDownloader JSON, yt-dlp live_chat.json or chat-downloader JSON) and keeps it with a recording's analyses, so highlights.find counts busy chat and emotes. Nothing is uploaded. |
| `highlights_toReel` | Make Highlight Reel | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a new sequence from highlight moments (the sequence's highlight markers, or "moments"): each moment with handles, best first up to "count" / "maxDuration", in time or score order, with transitions between them. With "music" the cuts land on its beats (every "beatsPerCut" beats) and the music plays under the reel; "slowMotion" slows the moment's peak. One undo step. |
| `highlights_toShort` | Make Highlight Short | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes one highlight moment (a highlight marker by rank, or start/end) a vertical 1080x1920 Short: the moment cut out with every track, laid out with layout.apply ("verticalSplit" with the facecam under the gameplay when there is one: a facecam clip above the gameplay or "facecamRegion"; else "verticalBlurFill": the whole game view over a blurred copy), captioned (the "Shorts" caption style unless "captionPreset" says otherwise), with the moment's title as the hook and loudness for Shorts. One undo step. |
| `history_checkpoint` | Save Version | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Records the project as it is now in the version history (unchanged since the last version: nothing is added). Give "label" to name it ("Client cut v2"): named versions are never pruned. Hosts call it on save, every few minutes of editing and before an AI agent applies a plan (kind). |
| `history_diff` | Compare Versions | read | What changed from one version to another ("current" is the project as it is): per sequence the clips added, removed, moved, trimmed or retimed, effects and keyframes changed, settings, tracks, markers and captions; media and review notes. "summary" says it in lines with timecodes. |
| `history_export` | Save Version As | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a saved version as a project file of its own ("restore as a new project"). Refuses to replace a file unless "overwrite". |
