| `history_list` | Version History | read | The project's saved versions, oldest first, as arrays: id, createdAt (UTC), kind (save, auto, agent, manual, restore), label (named versions are kept), sequences, clips, the bytes the version added. |
| `history_name` | Name Version | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Names a saved version (an empty label unnames it). Named versions are kept when the history prunes. |
| `history_restore` | Restore Version | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Goes back to a saved version: the whole project (one undo step; the project as it was is saved as a version first), or, with "sequence", that sequence of the version as a new sequence next to the current ones (the media it plays is the project's own where the project still has it). The no-cloud lock stays on. |
| `interchange_export` | Export Timeline | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes the sequence (with the sequences it nests and its multicam sources) as a timeline file other editors read, at "path": Final Cut Pro 7 XML ("fcp7-xml": Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve), FCPXML ("fcpxml": Final Cut Pro, Resolve; "fcpxmlVersion" 1.10 or 1.11), OpenTimelineIO ("otio") or a CMX3600 EDL ("edl"); or for audio post as an AAF ("aaf": Pro Tools, Nuendo, Resolve / Fairlight, Media Composer) or an OMF 2.0 file ("omf") with its audio rendered to new files ("audioPost": Premiere's AAF and OMF settings). Returns the export report: how many elements were carried exactly, and every one approximated (rounded to frames, a transition the format has no name for, ...) or dropped (graphics and effects the format cannot describe). The project does not change; a dry run writes nothing. |
| `keyframes_move` | Move Keyframes | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves several keyframes of one parameter together by a timeline distance, keeping their spacing. The distance is clamped so the keys stay within the clip (keys already outside it do not move further out); a moved key landing on another key replaces it. Returns the moved keys' new indices. |
| `keyframes_setInterpolation` | Set Keyframe Interpolation | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the interpolation (hold, linear, bezier, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut) of several keyframes of one parameter at once. |
| `layout_apply` | Apply Layout | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Lays out a gameplay clip and a facecam in one step, with plain editable clip settings: "pip" (gameplay fills the frame, the facecam in a corner with rounded corners or a circle, a border and a drop shadow), "verticalSplit" (9:16: gameplay on top, facecam below, or the other way round) or "verticalBlurFill" (9:16: the gameplay fitted to the width over a blurred copy of itself filling the frame, an optional facecam on top). The facecam is a clip on a track above the gameplay's, or "facecamRegion": the part of the capture where the webcam already shows (a copy of the gameplay cropped to it). Copies of the gameplay go on free tracks above it (new tracks when none is free) and are linked with it. Applying again replaces the layout's own effects. One undo step. Make a Shorts sequence first with sequence.create preset "shorts". |
| `layout_list` | List Layouts | read | The layout presets layout.apply takes and their options with defaults: facecam picture-in-picture and the vertical 9:16 shorts layouts. |
| `llm_local_models` | Local assistant models | read | Inspect the managed local assistant and its installable models; never downloads implicitly. |
| `llm_local_start` | Local assistant start | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Start or stop the managed local assistant (an installed, allow-listed model); never downloads implicitly. |
| `llm_local_status` | Local assistant status | read | Inspect the managed local assistant and its installable models; never downloads implicitly. |
| `llm_local_stop` | Local assistant stop | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Start or stop the managed local assistant (an installed, allow-listed model); never downloads implicitly. |
| `lottie_import` | Import Lottie | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Imports a Lottie animation (Bodymovin JSON from After Effects, LottieFiles) as a motion graphic: from a file ("path") or the JSON itself ("data"). | `lut_export` | Export .cube | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a clip's colour grade as a 3D LUT .cube file (Premiere's Lumetri panel > Export .cube): "size" points per side (default 33, as Premiere), display-referred Rec.709 in and out, evaluated at "time" (default the clip's middle). Outputs are clamped to 0..1. Refuses to replace a file unless "overwrite"; a dry run writes nothing. |
| `lut_import` | Import LUT | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Adds a .cube LUT file (1D or 3D, up to 65 points per side) to the project as an asset: it relinks and is collected like media. | `lut_list` | List LUTs | read | The built-in looks and camera input LUTs (with where their math comes from) and the project's LUT assets (path, offline, how many effects use each). |
| `marker_add` | Add Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a sequence marker. Premiere's marker colours are 0-7: green, red, purple, orange, yellow, white, blue, cyan. |
| `marker_clearAll` | Clear All Markers | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes every marker of the sequence (Premiere's Clear All Markers). |
| `marker_clearInAndOut` | Clear In and Out | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Clears the sequence In and Out marks. |
| `marker_list` | List Markers | read | The sequence's markers in time order with all their fields: index (what marker.update and marker.remove take), start, duration, name, comment, colour, type, web link, and the highlight a highlight finder wrote (score, confidence, reasons, peak, source; null when none). |
| `marker_markIn` | Mark In | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the sequence In mark at the start of the frame at a time. |
| `marker_markOut` | Mark Out | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the sequence Out mark at the end of the frame at a time (the frame is included). |
| `marker_remove` | Remove Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes the sequence marker at an index (as listed by sequence.summary). |
| `marker_update` | Edit Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes the sequence marker at an index (as listed by sequence.summary): any of its time, duration, name, comment, colour, type, URL and frame target. Keys left out keep their values; the markers stay sorted by start. |
| `mask_add` | Add Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a mask to a clip: to an effect ("effect"; the effect then only changes the masked area - a local correction, including the colour grade) or, without "effect", to the clip's opacity mask (it cuts the clip out). | `mask_list` | List Masks | read | A clip's masks by effect, with their parameters (keys at media times) and paths. |
| `mask_objectSelect` | Select Object | edit (`--allow-edit`) | AI Object Mask: segments the person or object you click on (positive and negative clicks), draw a box around, or name ("subject": a face, a person, a car...) on a frame of a clip with SAM 2.1 (local, on this computer), and tracks it through the shot. | `mask_propagate` | Track Object Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Tracks an object mask's object through the clip (or In / Out) from its last clicked frame: after a selection made with "propagate": "none", or across a shot cut with acrossShots. A job with progress; one undo step. |
| `mask_refine` | Refine Object Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | More clicks (positive: part of the object; negative: not) or a new box on a frame of an object mask: segments it again there and re-tracks from that frame. One undo step. |
| `mask_remove` | Remove Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a mask from its effect. |
| `mask_update` | Update Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a mask: only the fields given (name, shape, mode, inverted, enabled, params, path / pathKeys). A number replaces an animated parameter; {"keys": [...]} replaces its keys. |
| `media_browse` | Media Browser | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Media Browser listing of a folder: a camera card (AVCHD, Canon XF, P2, XDCAM EX / HD, XAVC) or a folder inside one lists the card's clips instead of its folders, a recording split into several files (a spanned clip, GoPro chapters) as one clip; any other folder its subfolders and media files. Each entry: folder or clip, name, path (a clip's first file), its files, the card, P2's audio channel files, bytes. |
| `media_duplicate` | Duplicate | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Edit > Duplicate on a project item: another item for the same file (or title, synthetic item) with its settings, Source Monitor marks, clip markers and metadata, in the same bin, named "<name> Copy" unless "name" is given. Clips in sequences keep playing the original. createdIds: the new item. |
| `media_fileMetadata` | File Metadata | read | The XMP of a media item's file (the Metadata panel's File section): a sidecar "<name>.xmp" first, else the packet inside the file, each property with its schema. |
| `media_importCameraClips` | Import from Media Browser | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Imports clips as the Media Browser lists them (media.browse): each "files" entry is a clip's first file; a spanned clip imports as ONE item playing its parts in turn, a P2 clip as a merged clip of its picture and its audio channel files (Merge Clips). Into "bin" (default the root). "copyTo": a folder - Premiere's Ingest (Copy): each clip's files are copied into <copyTo>/<clip name>/ first and the copies imported, so the card can be taken out. Clip markers the host reads from the files (the app and the CLI: a recording's chapter markers, as File > Import adds them) come in with the items; "markers" counts them. One undo step. |
| `media_importImageSequence` | Import Image Sequence | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Import with "Image Sequence" ticked: the numbered stills starting at "path" (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, DPX, Targa, OpenEXR or BMP; that file and the ones numbered after it without a gap, e.g. shot_0001.png, shot_0002.png, ...) become one video media item playing one still per frame at "frameRate" (default 29.97 fps, Premiere's Indeterminate Media Timebase), named after its first file, in "bin" (default the root). Returns its id, the frame count and the rate. |
| `media_importLayeredFile` | Import Layered File | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Import Layered File for a Photoshop file (.psd / .psb). "as": "mergeAll" (default: one picture of every visible layer), "merged" (one picture of the "layers" chosen), "layers" (Individual Layers: one item per chosen layer, named "<layer>/<file>", in a new bin named after the file) or "sequence" (the same items, plus a sequence of the document's size with one layer per video track, bottom layer on V1, each "duration" seconds long, default 5). "footage": "document" (default: each layer on the document's canvas, where it sits) or "layer" (Layer Size: cropped to the layer's pixels; in a sequence each clip is placed where the layer sits). "layers": layer indices from media.layeredFileInfo (default every visible layer). The items read the file each time they are opened, so saving it in Photoshop updates them. One undo step. |
| `media_interpretFootage` | Interpret Footage | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Modify > Interpret Footage on items: "frameRate" assumes that rate for the file's frames (a 120, 144 or 240 fps game capture as 30 or 60 fps plays every frame in slow motion: its clips, new and placed, run at that speed through the speed engine and its frame interpolation; placed clips keep their source In and grow into the gap after them), "pixelAspect" conforms the pixel aspect ratio, "fieldOrder" the fields, and "ignoreAlpha" / "invertAlpha" / "premultiplication" the alpha channel. A field that is absent keeps its interpretation; null goes back to what the file says. |
| `media_layeredFileInfo` | Layered File Info | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | What Premiere's Import Layered File dialog lists for a Photoshop file (.psd / .psb): the document's size, bit depth (8, 16 or 32) and colour mode (rgb, cmyk - converted to RGB on import - or grayscale) and its layers bottom to top - index, name, visibility (its own eye and its groups'), whether it has pixels or is a group, its bounds in document pixels, blend mode and the groups holding it. |
| `media_list` | List Media | read | Lists the project's media as arrays in mediaFields order: id, name, duration in ms, whether it has video, its number of audio streams, whether it is a still image and whether it is offline. |
| `media_makeOffline` | Make Offline | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Make Offline (Project panel; the media files remain on disk): the items go offline - their clips show Media Offline - until they are linked again (File > Relink). Titles and other generated items have no file and are refused. |
| `media_makeSubclip` | Make Subclip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | A new media item playing "in".."out" (exclusive) of a media item's file, named "name", in "bin" (default the root). Restricted (default) keeps trims inside that range. Returns its id. |
| `media_mergeClips` | Merge Clips | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Merge Clips: a merged clip of a video clip and separately recorded audio, synced by their In points, Out points, timecode, first clip markers or audio waveforms ("audio" needs the host's audio analysis). It is a synced source (a merged multicam source: the camera as angle 1, each recorder as another); edited into a sequence it shows the camera and plays every recording (and the camera's sound unless "removeCameraAudio"), and trims, ripples and undoes like any clip; multicam.flatten turns a clip of it into the items' own linked clips. createdIds: the merged clip. |
| `media_newSynthetic` | New Synthetic Item | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a synthetic project item (File > New): "barsAndTone" (SMPTE colour bars, params pattern 0 HD RP 219 or 1 SD EG 1, with a sine tone: tone.frequency, tone.level), "blackVideo", "colorMatte" (params color.r/g/b, 0..1: a background for text, a flash), "countingLeader" (Premiere's Universal Counting Leader: 8 seconds counting down from 8 to 2 with a clock wipe, its colours and cue blips as params) or "transparentVideo" (a layer of its own for effects that draw). It is made for the sequence's frame size and rate, needs no file and can be any length (the leader is 8 seconds). Put it on the timeline with clip.overwrite or clip.insert. createdIds: the item. |
| `media_rawSourceSettings` | RAW Source Settings | read | The Source Settings a camera RAW item (ProRes RAW, CinemaDNG) is developed with: "raw" whether the item is camera RAW at all, "exposure" in stops, "whiteBalance" "asShot" (the camera's) or "custom" with the "temperature" (K) and "tint" of the light it is balanced for. |
| `media_readXmp` | Read XMP Metadata | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Fills the clip metadata of media items from the XMP of their files (Premiere's links: Scene, Shot, Take, Log Note, Good, Client, Tape Name, Comment, Description and the camera fields). "overwrite" (default true) replaces what is set; false only fills empty fields. Items without XMP stay. One undo step. |
| `media_replaceFootage` | Replace Footage | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Replace Footage (Project panel): the item plays another file from now on - every clip of it keeps its place, source times, effects and markers, and its marks, markers and settings stay; the old file's proxy is dropped. "rename" (default true) gives the item the new file's name. Refused when a clip would play past the new file's end or the file lacks a stream a clip plays. Needs a host that reads media files (the app, wabcut-cli). |
| `media_setAttributes` | Media Attributes | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Library metadata of media items: name (new clips take it; existing clips keep theirs), label colour, comment, description, poster frame (a source time, or null to clear it) and (0.2) Premiere's clip metadata: scene, shot, take, log note, client, good, tape name, status and the camera fields (camera angle, label and model, shot date and location). Fields not given stay. One undo step for any number of items. |
| `media_setRawSourceSettings` | Source Settings | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Modify > Source Settings for camera RAW items (ProRes RAW, CinemaDNG): develops the items with "exposure" (stops, -5 to +5) and a white balance - "asShot" (the camera's) or "custom": the "temperature" (2000 to 15000 K; lower turns the picture bluer) and "tint" (-100 to +100, toward magenta) of the light to balance for, from the as-shot light (ProRes RAW's temperature; 6500 K for CinemaDNG). Absent fields keep the first item's. Playback, thumbnails and export all develop the items so; their proxies are dropped (made from the old development). Items that are not camera RAW are refused. One undo step. |
| `media_setScaling` | Default Media Scaling | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the default media scaling of media items (Premiere's Preferences > Media > Default Media Scaling, which Premiere applies to items as they are imported): how later insert / overwrite edits and drops size their video clips in a sequence of another frame size - "none" (pixel size), "scaleToFrameSize", "setToFrameSize" or "setToFillFrame". Clips already in sequences keep their size. |
| `media_setSubclip` | Edit Subclip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a subclip's range and restriction (Premiere's Edit Subclip). Restricting is refused while a clip of it uses media outside the new range. |
| `media_setTimecode` | Modify Timecode | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Clip > Modify > Timecode on items: the timecode of the first frame ("timecode" in the item's frame rate, or ticks; null: the file's own) and the reel (tape) name. Multicam and Merge Clips sync by it, and the Source Monitor shows it. |
| `multicam_angles` | Multicam Angles | read | A multicam source's angles: their names, tracks and sync offsets, and how they were synced. |
| `multicam_autoSwitch` | Auto Switch Multicam | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Cuts a multicam clip to whoever is speaking, on this computer: the active speaker's close-up after a minimum hold, cut a little before they start, the wide shot for crosstalk, laughter, long pauses and for variety on long monologues, optional reaction shots, never in the middle of a word. Presets: calm (podcast), interview, energetic; every rule tunable. The result is ordinary angle cuts (editable afterwards), one undo step, each with its reason ("Cut to Cam B: Speaker 2 starts talking"); dryRun previews them. |
| `multicam_create` | Create Multi-Camera Source Sequence | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Create Multi-Camera Source Sequence: a new sequence with one angle per media item (its video on a video track, each audio stream on an audio track) synced by "sync": their start timecodes, Source Monitor In or Out marks, first clip markers, audio waveforms (needs the host's audio analysis) or "offsets" given by hand. Cut it into a sequence with sequence.insert / overwrite "sourceSequence". |
| `multicam_flatten` | Flatten | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Flatten: a multicam clip (with its linked multicam partners) is replaced by the clips of the angles it plays, trimmed to what it shows (audio angles' tracks on its audio track and the ones below). Refused when that would not look and sound the same (effects on it, retimed, a clip in the way). |
| `multicam_setSync` | Set Angle Sync | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves one angle of a multicam source in time (its sync offset: where its material starts); every multicam clip then shows that angle shifted. The source's sync method becomes manual. |
| `multicam_switchAngle` | Switch Multicam Angle | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's angle switch (the 1-9 keys while playing): the multicam clip is cut at "at" and plays "angle" from there to its next cut; without "at" the whole clip switches. "switches" records a list of [time, angle] switches (a live multicam edit) as one undo step. "target": the picture, the sound or both (default). |
| `narration_create` | Narration | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Narration from a script with the user's own voice provider (BYOK): each line spoken, over its rough-cut beat when the sequence is a rough cut (AI-11) or one after another, on a new "Narration" audio track with the Dialogue role and the other audio ducked under it, as one undo step. The audio is marked AI-generated. Paid: "estimate" prices it; a run needs "maxCost" and the app's approval. |
| `plugins_list` | List Audio Plugins | read | The audio plugins (CLAP, VST3) this computer has, by effect id ("plugin.vst3.<class id>", "plugin.clap.<plugin id>"): name, vendor, version, category, latency (frames), whether it has an editor, and with "params" its parameters (keys "p<id>", ranges, automatable). Put one on clips or tracks with clip.addEffect / audio.addEffect ("plugin"); its parameters are keyframed like any effect's. Also the blocklist (plugins that crashed or hung while scanned) and the folders scanned. |
| `project_importItems` | Import from Project | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's import of a project (or of selected sequences): copies of another project's bins (with everything in them), sequences (with what they play: media, nested and multicam sequences, LUTs, speakers, transcript corrections, redactions, review notes, templates and styles this project lacks) and media items, in "into" (default the root) or a new bin "binName". Media this project already has (same file) is reused, so no item is duplicated; files are found where the other project is. "everything" brings the whole project. The copies remember the other project and their id there (importSource: Reveal in Source Project, relinks offered). One undo step. |
| `project_merge` | Merge Projects | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Three-way merge of another copy of this project ("theirs", a project file) into this one, both edited from "base" (the file they started from): edits of different sequences, tracks or clips merge; the same thing changed differently on both sides is a conflict with a stable id. With unresolved conflicts the result is only staged (the project does not change; the conflicts and what would change are returned) unless "apply"; "choices" resolves them ([{conflict: id, take: "mine" \| "theirs"}]; unresolved ones keep mine). A merge that cannot give a valid project with those choices is staged too, with "invalid" saying why. One undo step. |
| `project_summary` | Project Summary | read | Lists the project's sequences (id, rate, length, track and clip counts) and media counts. Start here. |
| `provenance_report` | Generated media provenance | read | Unsigned report of generated segments; no prompts or credentials. |
| `record_takes` | Voice-over Takes | read | The takes of a recorded voice-over slot (Premiere's repeated voice-over passes over one range): each pass over the same track and range made a media item in the Voice-over bin, and the clip plays the newest unless record.useTake chose another. Lists them newest first with their number, media, start, length, input device, time and which one the clip plays. |
| `record_useTake` | Use Voice-over Take | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Plays another take of a recorded voice-over slot (record.takes): that take's media goes over its recorded range on the clip's track as an overwrite, with the clip's level, pan and effects. The takes stay in the Voice-over bin. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `redaction_add` | Add Redaction | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Marks a region of a media item in SOURCE time for privacy: every use of that range in every sequence (trimmed, sped up, reversed, reused) is blurred, pixelated or covered in preview, export and burn-in, before the clip's own effects; "audio" mutes or bleeps it (only "words" when given). Mark by "media" + "source", or through a "clip" between "in" and "out". The region can be keyframed or tracked (track.mask on a clip's mask, then copied) - its key times are media times. Returns the redaction's id. |
| `redaction_detectFaces` | Redact Faces | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Finds every face of a media item (or a clip's part of it) with the face detector on this computer, follows each one and covers it with its own source-anchored redaction (blur, mosaic or solid) that moves with it: every use of the media in every sequence is covered. Fail closed: a face seen once is redacted, with a margin. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `redaction_list` | List Redactions | read | The project's redactions (of one media item with "media"). |
| `redaction_override` | Redaction Override | edit (`--allow-edit`) | "Don't redact here": the redaction skips this clip (and, with "linked", its linked partners), or applies again with "redact": true. A clip later cut from an excepted one is redacted again until excepted too. |
| `redaction_remove` | Remove Redaction | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a redaction everywhere. |
| `redaction_update` | Update Redaction | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a redaction: only the fields given. |
| `reframe_createSequence` | Auto Reframe | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a copy of a sequence at another aspect ("9:16" for vertical shorts, "1:1", "4:5", "16:9") whose video clips keep their subjects in frame: per shot, a smooth virtual camera (still, then steady pans) follows the main subject, all faces, the speaker or an anchor. The result is ordinary, editable Position/Scale keyframes on each clip (nothing is rendered); the source sequence is not changed. Run analysis.subjects first for long media (otherwise this runs it). The new sequence remembers its source, so reframe.rerun can make it again. |
| `reframe_rerun` | Reframe Again | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a reframed sequence again from its source sequence (after the source was edited), with the parameters it was made with, or new ones given here. It replaces the reframed sequence's contents (its manual keyframe changes too); its id, name and bin stay. Fails when the source sequence was deleted. |
| `render_deletePreviewFiles` | Delete Render Files | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Deletes preview files: of the sequence between "start" and "end" (In to Out with Sequence > Delete Render Files In to Out), of the whole sequence, or with "all" of every sequence in the project. The edit itself is not affected; the segments show red or yellow again. Needs a host with a preview cache; a dry run lists what would be deleted. |
| `render_previewInOut` | Render In to Out | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Renders preview files for the red and yellow segments between In and Out (or "start" / "end"; else the whole sequence), so they play in real time; segments with a valid preview are skipped. The cache keys each file by the segment's content and drops it when an edit changes that content. Needs a host with a preview renderer (the app); a dry run lists the segments it would render. |
| `render_status` | Render Bar | read | The render bar of a sequence (Premiere's red/yellow/green bar): segments between edit points, each "red" (must be rendered to play in real time: nested sequences, adjustment layers or effects heavier than real time), "yellow" (effects, transitions, blend modes or track mattes that may play in real time), "rendered" (a valid preview file exists) or "none" (plays as it is). Rendered segments show only in hosts with a preview cache. |
| `review_add` | Add Review Note | edit (`--allow-edit`) | A frame-accurate comment on the sequence: at "time" (a frame) or from "start" to "end", optionally pointing at a spot or rectangle of the frame ("mark"), by "author". Returns its id. |
| `review_exportPackage` | Export Review Package | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a review package folder for a client or reviewer: notes.json (the notes with timecodes) and index.html (one self-contained page with a thumbnail per note, its mark drawn on it), plus the thumbnails in frames/. Notes: the sequence's ("sequence"; all the project's without it), or "status" only. Thumbnails come from the host's renderer, else placeholder cards. |
| `review_importPackage` | Import Review Package | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Reads a review package's notes back (one undo step): replies and status update the matching notes (by id, else by sequence, time and text), new notes are added at their timecodes, and notes that cannot be placed or that changed on both sides are listed as conflicts and left out. |
| `review_list` | Review Notes | read | The review notes of the sequence ("sequence"; all the project's without it), in time order, with their timecodes, mark, author, status and replies ([author, text, createdAt]). |
| `review_remove` | Delete Review Note | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a note and its replies. |
| `review_reply` | Reply to Review Note | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a reply to a note's thread. |
| `review_resolve` | Resolve Review Note | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Marks a note resolved (or open again with "resolved": false). |
| `review_toMarkers` | Review Notes to Markers | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Turns the sequence's review notes ("notes", or all of them) into sequence markers: named after the note's first line, the comment holding the text, author and replies, red while open, green once resolved. With "remove" the notes go. |
| `roughcut_fromScript` | Rough Cut from Script | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a first cut from a script, an outline or bullet points: each line is found in the transcripts of the recordings (fuzzy, Thai too), the best take of it chosen (fewest fillers and false starts, complete sentence, clean audio; alternates kept), and the takes assembled in script order as a new sequence with linked video and audio trimmed to the words with small handles. Optional: clean-up of fillers and pauses, B-roll suggestions on their own track. Returns the alignment report (per line: the chosen take, its confidence, the alternates). Needs transcripts. One undo step; dryRun previews it. |
| `roughcut_swapTake` | Swap Take | edit (`--allow-edit`) | In a rough cut made by roughcut.fromScript, plays another recorded take of one line in place of the current one; what follows moves to fit (a ripple). The report of roughcut.fromScript numbers the lines and their takes. |
| `scopes_read` | Read Scopes | read | Scope statistics of the picture at a time (or of one clip alone): luma percentiles in IRE, clipped highlights and crushed blacks, mean colour, saturation and colour cast, with a verdict ("underexposed", "overexposed", "low contrast", "clipped highlights", "crushed blacks" or "ok"). Read only. |
| `search_footage` | Search Footage | read | Smart search: finds the moments of the project's media that show or say what the query describes ("a dog on the beach", "the part where she mentions the budget", Thai too), by what the frames show (an image-text model) and what is said (the transcripts). Returns hits best first: the media, its source range (sourceIn / sourceOut in ticks, start / end in seconds) ready for clip.insert, the matched transcript words and a score. Media must be indexed first (search.indexMedia); a read, it changes nothing. |
| `search_indexMedia` | Index Media for Search | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Brings the smart-search index up to date for some or all media: keyframes of every shot (one per shot, more in long shots) through the image-text model, and the transcript's phrases. Unchanged files are skipped, so running it again is cheap. Runs locally; nothing leaves the computer. |
| `sequence_addEdit` | Add Edit | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Add edit / razor (Premiere Ctrl+K): cuts the clips under a time on the given tracks (default: the targeted tracks). |
| `sequence_addEditToAllTracks` | Add Edit to All Tracks | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Add edit to all tracks (Premiere Ctrl+Shift+K): cuts every unlocked track at a time. |
| `sequence_addSubmixTrack` | Add Audio Submix Track | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds an audio submix track (Premiere's Sequence > Add Tracks > Audio Submix Tracks): a bus that audio tracks are assigned to (track.setOutput) or send to (track.addSend). Its own effects (audio.addEffect with the submix as the target), fader and panner (track.setVolume / track.setPan), mute and solo (track.setState) apply to the sum, and it outputs to the Mix. Submixes are labelled S1, S2, ... A mono submix folds its input to mono and pans it; the format is fixed once made. Use it to put one reverb or compressor on several tracks (all the voices, the music). sequence.removeTrack deletes one (its tracks go to the Mix). One undo step. |
| `sequence_addTrack` | Add Track | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a video track above the top video track or an audio track below the last audio track. |
| `sequence_applyAudioTransition` | Apply Audio Transition | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ctrl+Shift+D: a constant-power crossfade on the edit point nearest the playhead on each targeted audio track. |
| `sequence_applyDefaultTransitions` | Apply Default Transitions to Selection | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Shift+D: default transitions on both ends of each clip (cross dissolve on video, constant power on audio), on the cut where a neighbour meets the clip, otherwise a fade inside it. |
| `sequence_applyVideoTransition` | Apply Video Transition | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ctrl+D: a cross dissolve on the edit point nearest the playhead on each targeted video track, shortened to the media there is. |
| `sequence_beats` | List Beats | read | The beats of the sequence's beat grid as arrays in beatFields order: time, place in the bar (1 = downbeat) and index from the grid's downbeat. |
| `sequence_closeGap` | Close Gap | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Sequence > Close Gap: removes the empty time between the clips (with their linked partners) on their tracks - with no clips, every gap of the unlocked tracks from the sequence's start - only where none of those tracks has material, so linked clips stay in sync; other unlocked sync-locked tracks lose the same time, and a gap where one of them has material stays. Caption cues follow. One undo step. |
| `sequence_create` | New Sequence | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a new, empty sequence (3 video and 3 audio tracks, 48 kHz) from a preset (sequence.presets: "1080p60", "1440p144", "2160p60", "shorts" for 1080x1920 60 fps, ...). createdIds: the sequence. |
| `sequence_duplicate` | Duplicate Sequence | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Edit > Duplicate on a sequence in the Project panel: a copy of the whole sequence (tracks, clips, effects, markers, captions; new ids) in the same bin, named "<name> Copy" ("Copy 2", ... when taken) unless "name" is given. createdIds: the copy. |
| `sequence_exportFrame` | Export Frame | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Export Frame (the Program Monitor's camera button, Ctrl+Shift+E): renders the sequence frame at "time" as an export renders it (original media, the export colour transform) at the sequence's size and writes it to "path" as DPX (10-bit), JPEG, PNG, TIFF, Targa, BMP, GIF or OpenEXR (half float, linear). With "importIntoProject" the still is added to the project as a media item (one undo step); otherwise the project does not change. Needs a host that renders frames (the app, wabcut-cli); a dry run writes nothing. |
| `sequence_exportMarkers` | Export Markers | read | Returns the sequence's markers as text: "csv" (Premiere's columns: Marker Name, Description, In, Out, Duration, Marker Type, plus Color) or "youtube" (chapter lines for a video description, from the chapter markers, or every marker when there are none). YouTube's rules (the first chapter at 0:00, at least 3 chapters, each at least 10 s) are reported as warnings, never fixed silently. Nothing is written to disk. |
| `sequence_extract` | Extract | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Extract (Premiere "'"): removes a time range from the targeted tracks and closes the gap; sync-locked tracks lose the same range so they stay in sync. |
| `sequence_goToGap` | Go to Gap | read | Premiere's Sequence > Go to Gap: where the next (previous) gap after (before) "time" starts - in the sequence (a time no track has a clip in, before the last clip) or in a track ("scope": "track": a gap on any of "tracks", default the targeted tracks). data.time is null when there is none; hosts move the playhead there. |
| `sequence_joinThroughEdits` | Join Through Edits | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Join Through Edit (right-click a through edit) and Sequence > Join Through Edits: through edits - cuts between two pieces of the same clip that continue each other (same source, continuous source time, the same speed, effects and attributes, no transition at the cut) - at the edges of the clips (and their linked partners) go, each pair becoming one clip; with no clips, every through edit on the unlocked tracks. Refused when there is none there. |
| `sequence_lift` | Lift | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Lift (Premiere ';'): removes a time range from the targeted tracks and leaves a gap. |
| `sequence_makeSubsequence` | Make Subsequence | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Sequence > Make Subsequence (Shift+U): a new sequence with copies of the clips (and their linked partners) on the same tracks, the earliest at 0, with the transitions between them and the markers and caption cues over their span; with no clips, everything on the targeted tracks between In and Out (Make Subsequence from In to Out). The sequence is unchanged. Named "<sequence> Sub_01" unless "name" is given. createdIds: the subsequence. |
| `sequence_makeVersion` | Make Vertical or Square Version | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes a 9:16 Shorts (1080x1920) or 1:1 square (1080x1080) version of a 16:9 gaming edit as a new sequence: with a facecam (a track named like a webcam - facecam, webcam, cam, camera -, a picture-in-picture made with layout.apply, "facecamTrack" or "facecamRegion") Shorts get the vertical split (gameplay on top, facecam below) and square versions the gameplay over a blurred fill with the facecam in a corner; without one, Auto Reframe when the host has it, else the gameplay fitted to the width over a blurred copy of itself. Captions move into the version's safe area. The 16:9 sequence is not changed. One undo step. |
| `sequence_matchFrame` | Match Frame | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Match Frame (Premiere F): the clip under a time on the targeted tracks (the topmost; every track when none is targeted there), its media and the source frame shown. Like Premiere, the media's source marks become the clip's used range (setMarks false leaves them). |
| `sequence_nest` | Nest | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Nest: the clips (and, with "linked", their partners) move into a new sequence in the same bin, keeping their tracks, effects, links and the transitions between them, and one nested clip per kind (picture on the lowest selected video track, the mix on the lowest audio track, linked) takes their place. Returns the new sequence's id and the nested clips. |
| `sequence_newFromClip` | New Sequence From Clip | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's File > New > Sequence From Clip (the Project panel's right-click): a sequence whose settings match the item - frame size as it displays (a phone video turned 90 degrees makes a vertical sequence), frame rate (its interpretation when set), pixel aspect and audio sample rate - named after it, in its bin, with the item (between its Source Monitor marks) edited in at the start, picture on V1 and each audio stream on its own track. createdIds: the sequence. |
| `sequence_presets` | Sequence Presets | read | The sequence presets sequence.create and sequence.setSettings take (Premiere's rates for the target uses): landscape 720p, 1080p, 1440p and 4K at 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97 (also drop-frame), 30, 50, 59.94 (also drop-frame) and 60 fps, 1080p to 4K also at 120, 144 and 240 fps; vertical 1080x1920 for Shorts, TikTok and Reels ("shorts" at 60 fps, "shorts30", "vertical23.976" ...) and square 1080x1080. Every rate is exact in ticks. |
| `sequence_removeDeadTime` | Remove Dead Time | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Finds low-activity stretches of gameplay - game audio and picture motion both low (loading screens, walking, waiting) for at least "minSeconds" - and removes them with handles kept, like a silence cleanup. Without "apply" it only lists the ranges (the preview: nothing changes); review them, then call again with "apply": true (the same detection) or with the "ranges" to remove. Removing ripple-deletes on every unlocked track and the captions in one undo step; markers move with the material. Listens to the gameplay track (the lowest video track with media or a nested clip) and the unmuted audio tracks unless "tracks" says otherwise. Nested and multicam clips are measured through what they show and play (the active angle) and cut in place, staying nested / multicam. Media the host cannot measure is never cut. |
| `sequence_removeTrack` | Delete Track | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a track and its clips (their linked partners on other tracks stay, unlinked). The track must be unlocked. A submix track ("S1"): the tracks assigned to it output to the Mix and the sends to it are removed. |
| `sequence_reverseMatchFrame` | Reverse Match Frame | read | Reverse Match Frame (Premiere Shift+R): where a source frame is used in the sequence: the first use at or after "from", else the first one. |
| `sequence_rippleTrimNextToPlayhead` | Ripple Trim Next Edit to Playhead | edit (`--allow-edit`) | W: removes the time from the playhead to the next edit point on the targeted tracks and closes it. |
| `sequence_rippleTrimPreviousToPlayhead` | Ripple Trim Previous Edit to Playhead | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Q: removes the time from the previous edit point to the playhead on the targeted tracks and closes it. |
| `sequence_setBeatGrid` | Set Beat Grid | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the sequence's beat grid, which timeline snapping, edit.snapToBeats and edit.cutToBeats use: a tempo and the time of a downbeat, a tempo from tapped beats (at least two times), or detected beats; "clear" removes it. analysis.detectBeats sets it from the music. |
| `sequence_setMasterFormat` | Set Master Channel Format | edit (`--allow-edit`) | The sequence's master: stereo, or 5.1 (mono and stereo tracks through their 5.1 panners; previewed on a stereo device and exported to stereo through an ITU-R BS.775 downmix; exports with 0 channels follow it). One undo step. |
| `sequence_setMasterGain` | Set Master Gain | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the master fader: dB, 0 = unity, applied to the sequence's mix after the master effects and before the meters (what export renders). With "time" it sets a keyframe there. One undo step. |
| `sequence_setPatches` | Set Source Patching | read | Checks a source patching (Premiere's source track indicators: which source track goes to which sequence track, and which are switched off) and returns it in order. Patching is view state of the app's Source Monitor, which keeps it; elsewhere nothing is stored: pass "patches" to the source edits. |
| `sequence_setSettings` | Sequence Settings | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Sequence > Sequence Settings on an existing sequence. "preset" (sequence.presets) sets the frame size, timebase and drop-frame display at once; the other fields override it. Changing the timebase of a sequence with clips keeps the edit in real time and puts every edit point on the new frame grid: clip starts and ends, transitions, markers, In/Out, the work area and caption cues move to the nearest frame (a clip without media to reach it gets the frame inside instead), clips keep the picture under them, adjacent clips stay adjacent and locked tracks are left alone. Frame size changes keep each clip's Motion. Drop-frame display applies at 29.97 and 59.94 only. "label" is the sequence's label colour (Premiere's Label: the Project panel and its timeline tab). "rippleMarkers" is Markers > Ripple Sequence Markers. One undo step. |
| `sequence_setTargets` | Set Track Targets | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Targets exactly the given tracks (Premiere's track targeting: Lift, Extract, paste, Up/Down navigation and Match Frame use them). |
| `sequence_settings` | Sequence Settings Info | read | A sequence's settings as Premiere's Sequence Settings shows them: timebase, frame size, pixel aspect, fields, audio sample rate, drop-frame display, preview file format, video and audio display formats and the start timecode. |
| `sequence_summary` | Sequence Summary | read | Compact view of a sequence: settings, In/Out marks, every track (label, id, flags) with its clips as arrays in clipFields order (times are timecodes; link = link group, clips with the same value are linked), and markers. Use from/to to look at part of a long sequence. |
| `sequence_unnest` | Unnest | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Resolve's Decompose: a nested clip (with its linked nested partners) is replaced by copies of the clips it shows - trimmed to what it shows, on its track and the ones above (audio: below), with their effects, links and transitions. Only when that looks and sounds exactly the same; otherwise it is refused with the reason (retimed, effects on the nested clip, track effects, a missing track, a clip in the way, ...). |
| `shorts_create` | Create Shorts | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes one new sequence per short (from shorts.find): the range cut out of the source sequence, reframed to 9:16 (or "aspect") with editable keyframes following the speaker, captioned (vertical shorts in the "Shorts" caption style unless "captionPreset" says otherwise), with the title as a hook for its first seconds; optionally cleaned of fillers and silences and normalised to -14 LUFS. The source is not changed; all the shorts of one call are one undo step. Export them afterwards (vertical 1080x1920). |
| `shorts_find` | Find Shorts | read | Finds the best moments of a long sequence for vertical shorts (20-90 s each): whole sentences, a hook in the first seconds, one topic, lively delivery, faces, few fillers; optionally about a topic ("query"). Returns them best first with a score breakdown, reasons, a suggested title, the words and a start/end (seconds; ticks too) snapped to sentences and cuts, ready for shorts.create. Needs the media's transcripts. A read: it changes nothing. |
| `source_addMarker` | Add Clip Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a clip marker to a media item, in media time. Every clip of the media shows it where it uses that part of the source (Premiere's master clip markers). |
| `source_clearMarks` | Clear Source Marks | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Clears a media item's source In and/or Out mark (Premiere's Source Monitor Clear In / Clear Out / Clear In and Out). |
| `source_exportFrame` | Export Frame (Source Monitor) | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Export Frame from the Source Monitor: the frame of a media item at a source time, at the media's own frame size, written to "path" in the chosen format (as sequence.exportFrame); with "importIntoProject" the still joins the project (one undo step). Needs a host that renders frames. |
| `source_load` | Load Source | read | Opens a media item as the source (Premiere's Source Monitor): its kind, duration, frame rate, stored In/Out marks and the source patching a source edit would use. The app also shows it in its Source Monitor. |
| `source_removeMarker` | Remove Clip Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a media item's clip marker at an index. |
| `source_setMarks` | Set Source Marks | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets a media item's source In/Out marks (Premiere's Source Monitor I and O). They are saved with the project and used by edit.insertFromSource / overwriteFromSource. A key left out keeps its mark; null clears it; an In at or after the Out (or an Out at or before the In) clears the other mark. |
| `source_updateMarker` | Edit Clip Marker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a media item's clip marker at an index (keys left out keep their values). |
| `spelling_check` | Check Spelling | read | The misspelled words of a text in a language (default the user's), from the host's spell checker and the user's dictionary, as captions.checkSpelling lists them (byte ranges of the text). "available" is false when the host cannot check that language. |
| `takes_find` | Find Takes | read | Finds repeated attempts of the same line (retakes and false starts) in a sequence and the recordings it uses: groups of takes, best first, each with its words, a word-by-word difference from the best one, and quality (fillers, false starts, pauses, complete sentence, level, clipping, noise floor, pace). "improvable" groups would change with takes.use best. Needs transcripts. A read: it changes nothing. |
| `takes_use` | Use Take | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes the sequence say a line once, with the chosen take: other takes of it on the timeline are removed with their pause, and a take that is not on the timeline replaces the first one there (linked video and audio, with small handles; what follows moves to fit). "best": true does this for every group whose best take is not already the one heard. Pass the same options as takes.find (and its expectedRevision). One undo step; returns the review list. |
| `template_export` | Export Template | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Writes a template (template.list: the project's, the user's or a built-in) to a Wabcut template file (".wabcut-template.json") another Wabcut imports with template.import. Refuses to replace a file unless "overwrite"; a dry run writes nothing. |
| `template_import` | Import Motion Graphics Template | edit, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Adds a template file to the project's library (default) or the user's: a Wabcut template file (".wabcut-template.json", template.export) as it is, or a Motion Graphics template (".mogrt") made in Premiere Pro, approximately - its text Essential Properties become text fields of a lower third Wabcut lays out, the first colour the box's, checkboxes show it; the report lists what was approximated or dropped. Templates made in After Effects are refused (Wabcut cannot run After Effects compositions: export them as Lottie). Files are untrusted: the ZIP is read bounded, with no path leaving it. |
| `template_instantiate` | Add Template | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a graphic made from a template (template.list) as a clip, with field values (by field id: text a string, colour "#RRGGBB" or [r, g, b, a] 0..1 or {"brand": name}, font a family or {"family", "style", "weight"}, image a media id or name, duration a time, checkbox true/false). Its length: a "clip" duration field, else "duration", else the template's. The project's library is searched first, then the user's, then the built-ins (template.list). |
| `template_list` | Templates | read | The graphic templates of the project's library, the user's and the built-in ones that ship with Wabcut (C.16: gaming lower thirds, banners, callouts, stingers, end cards...; 0.4: essay and documentary name and title, location, quote, source and chapter cards that follow the brand kit): id, name, version, default length, canvas, and the fields (id, label, kind, default value) template.instantiate and template.setField take. Built-ins also give their category and "posterTime" (the design time a thumbnail shows: template.resolve draws it). With "id", that template only, with its graphic. |
| `template_resolve` | Template Draw List | read | The draw list of a template at a design time, without adding it to a timeline: what template browsers draw for thumbnails and hover previews (C.16). Default time: the template's poster time (everything has animated in). "values" previews field values. Same items as graphic.resolve. |
| `template_save` | Save as Template | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Saves a graphic clip's graphic as a template with editable fields (Premiere's Motion Graphics Templates): into the project's library (default), or the user's template library folder ("library": "user"; the host's, not a path). Saving under an id in use replaces that template and raises its version. |
| `template_setField` | Edit Template Fields | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets field values of a template instance clip (template.list shows the fields): "field" and "value", or several at once in "values" - one undo step. A "clip" duration field trims the clip's end. |
| `textStyle_apply` | Apply Text Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Gives text layers of a graphic clip a project text style; they follow it (updating the style restyles them). |
| `textStyle_create` | Create Text Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Create Text Style: the look of a text layer (its first run's font, size, fill, tracking...; its alignment, background and shadow) saved in the project under a name; the layer follows it. |
| `textStyle_list` | Text Styles | read | The project's text styles (Premiere's Text Style items): each with its look (the text JSON of a layer with one run: font, size, fill, tracking...; alignment, background; shadow) and how many text layers follow it. |
| `textStyle_remove` | Delete Text Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a project text style: the layers that followed it keep their look and follow nothing. |
| `textStyle_rename` | Rename Text Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames a project text style; the layers that follow it follow the new name. |
| `textStyle_update` | Push to Text Style | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Updates a project text style - Premiere's Push to Text Style - from a text layer's current look ("clip" and "layer") or from its JSON ("style", as textStyle.list gives it), and restyles every text layer of every graphic clip that follows it. Makes the style when there is none of that name. |
| `timeRemap_addHold` | Add Hold Segment | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Holds the frame shown at a timeline time for a duration inside a remapped clip; the rest of its remap plays later. |
| `timeRemap_addKey` | Add Time Remap Key | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a remap key at the sampled source position of a timeline time inside a remapped clip. Holds stay holds; the new key is otherwise linear and can reshape a smooth ramp. Returns its index. |
| `timeRemap_addReverse` | Add Reverse Segment | edit (`--allow-edit`) | From a timeline time inside a remapped clip, plays the media backwards at 100 % for a duration, then forwards again over the same frames (a boomerang); the rest of the remap plays later by twice the duration. Needs that much media before the point. |
| `timeRemap_enable` | Time Remapping | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Turns time remapping on (speed ramps, holds and reverse inside one clip; the clip shows the same frames, also beyond its ends for transitions and trims; keyframes of a clip that was not at 100 % then animate at timeline rate) or off (back to a constant speed: the one it shows if a single straight segment covers it, else 100 % from its first frame). Audio follows the remap (A.10): pitch kept (Maintain Audio Pitch, on by default when remapping starts) or varispeed; holds are silent. |
| `timeRemap_moveKey` | Move Time Remap Key | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves a remap key to another timeline time. Without "ripple" it stays between its neighbours and both segments around it change speed; with "ripple" the later keys move too, so only the segment before it changes speed (Premiere's speed keyframe drag). |
| `timeRemap_removeKey` | Remove Time Remap Key | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes a remap key (not the only one). |
| `timeRemap_setInterpolation` | Set Time Remap Interpolation | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Shapes the remap around keys: linear (constant speed between keys), hold (the frame holds until the next key, then jumps), or easeIn / easeOut / easeInOut / bezier for a smooth speed ramp. |
| `timeRemap_setKey` | Set Time Remap Key | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a remap key's source position, interpolation and Bezier handles together. Omitted fields keep their values. Slopes are source ticks per second of curve time (254016000000 = 100% forwards); influence is a fraction of the adjacent segment. Source bounds and monotonic segments are validated. |
| `timeRemap_setSpeed` | Set Segment Speed | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets the speed of one segment of a remapped clip (between two keys; the one playing at "time", or "segment" by index): its end key and the keys after it move, so later material plays earlier or later. |
| `timeline_removeSilences` | Remove Silences | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ripple-deletes a list of time ranges (e.g. silences found in a transcript) in one step. Only whole frames inside each range are removed. By default every track loses the same time so everything stays in sync; In/Out marks and track targeting are left as they were. |
| `timeline_rippleDelete` | Ripple Delete | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Ripple delete: removes clips and closes the time they used, or closes a gap. Sync-locked tracks lose the same time. A gap only closes when no sync-locked track has material in it. |
| `title_add` | New Title | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a text title as a clip on a video track: a title media item holding the text and font, and the clip's "wabcut.title.style" effect holding size, fill and stroke colours, stroke width, shadow, alignment, line spacing and tracking. Place, scale and rotate it with the clip's Transform (clip.setParam motion.*). "placement" chooses the track: the named one (overwriting; the default when "track" is given), the first free one at or above the named or targeted one (the default without "track": nothing under the title is overwritten), or a new track on top. createdIds: the clip, the style effect, the title media. |
| `title_setFont` | Set Title Font | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a title's font family and/or style. |
| `title_setText` | Edit Title Text | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Replaces a title's text. Every clip of the title shows the new text. |
| `track_addSend` | Add Track Send | edit (`--allow-edit`) | A send from an audio track to a submix (Premiere's Audio Track Mixer sends; at most 5 per track): a copy of the track's sound at its own level and pan, post-fader (follows the track's fader) unless "preFader". A muted or soloed-away track is silent in its sends too. Use it for a shared reverb: send each voice to a submix with the reverb. One undo step. |
| `track_mask` | Track Mask | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Tracks a mask through the clip's media, frame by frame from "time" (forward or backward, to the clip's end or "frames" frames), with pyramidal Lucas-Kanade on features inside the mask and a robust fit of its motion ("model"). Its transform.* parameters get ordinary keyframes (one undo step). Stops where the picture is lost (confidence below "minConfidence"); data lists each frame's confidence. A job: it reports progress and can be cancelled. |
| `track_removeSend` | Remove Track Send | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes send "send" (1..5) of an audio track; the later sends move up. One undo step. |
| `track_setFormat` | Set Track Channel Format | edit (`--allow-edit`) | An audio track's channel format (Premiere's mono, stereo, 5.1 and adaptive tracks): clips are mixed to it (mono averages, 5.1 to stereo is ITU-R BS.775), and it to the master's format; adaptive passes channels through one to one. One undo step. |
| `track_setOutput` | Set Track Output | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's track output assignment: where an audio track or a submix goes, "mix" (the master) or a submix track ("S1"). A submix cannot output into itself or into a submix that feeds it. One undo step. |
| `track_setPan` | Set Track Pan | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets an audio track's panner: -1 = left .. 0 = centre .. +1 = right, a balance on the track's stereo mix (centre leaves it unchanged; towards a side the other side follows the -3 dB constant-power curve down to silence). With "time" it sets a keyframe there. One undo step. |
| `track_setRecordArm` | Set Track Record Arm | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Arms an audio track for voice-over recording or disarms it (the R button of Premiere's track headers and Audio Track Mixer). The app's Record (record.start) records the microphone onto the armed track (else the targeted one) at the playhead or between the sequence In and Out; recording is the user's action in the app, never a command. Allowed on locked tracks; video tracks are refused. One undo step. |
| `track_setRole` | Set Track Role | edit (`--allow-edit`) | What an audio track carries: dialogue, music or effects (Premiere's Essential Sound types), or none. audio.autoDuck lowers music-role tracks under dialogue-role tracks. |
| `track_setSend` | Set Track Send | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes send "send" (1..5) of an audio track: its submix, pre- or post-fader, mute, level (dB) and pan; with "time" the level and pan given become keyframes there (send automation). One undo step. |
| `track_setState` | Set Track State | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes track header toggles: lock, target, sync lock, mute, solo, output, name. Unlocking is how a locked track becomes editable again. |
| `track_setSurroundPan` | Set Track 5.1 Panner | edit (`--allow-edit`) | The 5.1 panner of a mono or stereo track on a 5.1 master (Premiere's track 5.1 panner): the puck x (-1 left .. +1 right) and y (-1 back .. +1 front; front centre plays stereo on L/R and mono on C) and the LFE send in dB (-144 = off). One undo step. |
| `track_setVolume` | Set Track Volume | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Sets an audio track's fader (Premiere's track Volume): dB, 0 = unity, applied to the track's mix after its effects. With "time" it sets a keyframe there (track automation, in timeline time) instead of a constant; a constant replaces the track's volume keyframes. One undo step. |
| `track_transform` | Track Motion | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Tracks a region of a clip ("region": {x, y, width, height} 0..1 of the frame, {"mask": id}, or {"detect": "face"} once a detector is installed) and keys a clip's Motion with it (one undo step): "follow" moves "target" with the region (position; with the similarity model also scale and rotation), "stabilize" keys the tracked clip so the region stays still. A job: it reports progress and can be cancelled. |
| `transcript_addSpeaker` | New Speaker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a speaker to the project. Returns its id. |
| `transcript_assignSpeaker` | Assign Speaker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Says who speaks over a timeline range: the words the audio clips there play (on "track" only when given) belong to "speaker", or to a new speaker called "name". It wins over diarization and stays with the media when the clips are edited. |
| `transcript_cleanup` | Remove Fillers and Silences | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Removes every filler word and pause the review finds with at least minConfidence, in one undo step. |
| `transcript_correctRange` | Correct Words | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Fixes several consecutive words at once (they read "text", split over them by spaces). Like transcript.correctWord; the words must come from one media item. |
| `transcript_correctWord` | Correct Word | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Fixes a transcription mistake: the word reads "text" from now on, in the transcript the project sees and in captions generated or updated afterwards. The correction is saved with the project on top of the cached transcript, so transcribing again keeps it. |
| `transcript_corrections` | Transcript Corrections | read | The project's transcript corrections and how they apply to the current transcripts: applied, conflict (the words changed since, e.g. after re-transcription; the correction still wins), restored (no words there any more; the correction brings them back) or noTranscript. |
| `transcript_deleteRanges` | Delete Words | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes words (and pauses) like deleting text: ripple deletes on the tracks the words are heard on and their linked partners, cut on frame boundaries just outside the words, neighbouring deletions merged, sync-locked tracks following, locked tracks untouched. One undo step. |
| `transcript_export` | Export Transcript | read, files (`--allow-files`, confined) | Premiere's Export transcript as a text file: the sequence's transcript as paragraphs (split at speaker changes and pauses longer than maxPause) with their start and end timecodes and speaker. "txt": blocks of "start - end", the speaker, the text, a blank line between (transcript files captions.import reads back); "csv": Start,End,Speaker,Text rows; "docx": the .txt layout as a Word document (timecodes grey, speakers bold), which captions.import reads back too. Without "path" the text is returned (not for docx). Refuses to replace a file unless "overwrite"; a dry run writes nothing. |
| `transcript_find` | Find in Transcript | read | Premiere's Find for the transcript (the arrows of Find and Replace): every match of "find" (within a word, or across consecutive words when it has spaces) as the words it spans, the time of the first and their text, in transcript order. "matchCase" and "wholeWord" as transcript.findReplace. At most 1000 matches. |
| `transcript_findReplace` | Find and Replace in Transcript | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Premiere's Find and Replace for the transcript: every match of "find" (within a word, or across consecutive words when it has spaces) is corrected as transcript.correctRange would - saved with the project on top of the cached transcripts, so captions generated or updated later read it - in one undo step; with "words" (a match transcript.find listed) only that match (Premiere's Replace). "matchCase" and "wholeWord" as Premiere's options (without Match Case, Unicode simple case folding). A dry run lists the changes without making them. |
| `transcript_keepRanges` | Keep Only Words | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Rough cut: keeps the given word ranges and ripple-deletes everything else on the transcript's tracks, from the first to the last clip that has words. One undo step. |
| `transcript_mediaWords` | Media Transcript Words | read | One media item's words in source time (what the clip says before any edit: the Transcript panel's Source mode), as arrays in wordFields order: index, text, start and end as source timecodes in the media's rate and as ticks, speaker and recognition confidence. Corrections of the project apply; words inside an audio redaction read "[bleep]". Pick a soundbite, then source.setMarks with its first word's start and its last word's end and edit.insertFromSource / overwriteFromSource. audioStream: an index into the media's audio streams (default: the first one with a transcript). |
| `transcript_mergeSpeakers` | Merge Speakers | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Makes speakers one: every word, assignment and caption of "from" (one id or several) becomes "into", and the merged speakers go. |
| `transcript_moveRange` | Move Words | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Moves words (a sentence, a paragraph) to the word boundary before another word: cut out with a ripple and inserted there, with their linked video. One undo step. |
| `transcript_renameSpeaker` | Rename Speaker | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Renames a speaker and/or changes its colour. Name it by "speaker" id, or by the diarization "label" of a media item's transcript (transcript.speakers lists both); a label without a speaker gets one. |
| `transcript_review` | Review Fillers and Silences | read | Filler words (language-aware: um, uh, like in disfluent context; Thai อืม, เอ่อ, แบบว่า ...) and pauses longer than a threshold, as a review list: kind, word indices, time range, confidence, label and context. Remove chosen items with transcript.deleteRanges (fillers as words, silences as gaps) or all with transcript.cleanup. |
| `transcript_speakers` | Speakers | read | The project's speakers (id, name, colour, words in this sequence) and the diarization labels of the sequence's transcripts with the speaker each one is (null: none yet; transcript.renameSpeaker by media and label names one). |
| `transcript_text` | Transcript Text | read | What the sequence says, in timeline order, as paragraphs (split at speaker changes and pauses) with the word indices the other transcript commands take. Words inside an audio redaction read "[bleep]". Start here. |
| `transcript_transcribe` | Transcribe Media | analysis (`--allow-analysis`) | Transcribes the audio of media items or clips (default: every audio clip of the sequence) so the other transcript commands have words. provider: "auto" (on this computer when the local engine is built, else the user's cloud transcription model), "local", or "cloud:<model id>"; cloud transcription goes through the user's consent, spend cap and offline / no-cloud locks. Audio that already has a transcript is not transcribed again unless "force". "check": true only lists the providers and what has a transcript. Transcripts are stored per source file (the analysis cache), not in the project. |
| `transcript_words` | Transcript Words | read | The sequence's words in timeline order as arrays in wordFields order: index, text, timeline start and end, the audio clip and track it is heard on, speaker and recognition confidence. |
| `transition_add` | Add Transition | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Adds a transition at a clip's head or tail: on the cut when the neighbouring clip meets that edge, otherwise inside the clip (a fade from/to black). The media must have frames beyond the cut; by default the transition is shortened to what there is. Default effect: crossDissolve on video, constantPower on audio. |
| `transition_remove` | Remove Transition | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Deletes a transition; the edit point becomes a cut. |
| `transition_set` | Set Transition | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Changes a transition: its effect, parameters, its length on either side of the cut ("before", "after"), a new total "duration" placed by its alignment, or the alignment itself (which re-splits it; "custom" with "offset" puts the cut that far in). |
| `workflow_podcast` | Podcast Workflow | edit (`--allow-edit`) | The one-click podcast / interview edit, on this computer (local, free): sync the cameras and microphones (multicam by audio), lay out the episode (the multicam picture, each microphone on its own dialogue track), transcribe, Enhance Speech, loudness to -16 LUFS, remove fillers and long pauses, switch cameras to whoever speaks, captions, chapters from the topics (and YouTube chapters), optionally shorts. Without "run" it returns the plan (every step, on or off and why); with "run" it runs the enabled steps (or "steps"), as one undo step; "context" continues an earlier run. |
| `edit_batch` | Batch | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Applies several commands in order as ONE undo step: all of them or none. Later commands see the earlier ones' result. Read commands report in steps. |
| `edit_undo` | Undo | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Undoes the last change of this session (one edit or batch). |
| `edit_redo` | Redo | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Redoes the last undone change. |
| `project_save` | Save Project | edit (`--allow-edit`) | Writes the project file (atomically, keeping rotated .bak copies). With copyName, writes a copy next to it instead, e.g. "Rough cut v2.wabcut". |
